# Codex Pane Lifecycle Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** Execute this plan task by task with a fresh
> implementer and a specification-plus-quality review after every task. Track
> progress with the checkbox steps below.

## User Request

### Requested result
Freshell treats each coding-agent pane as one unit — its screen (the agent TUI in the PTY), its agent main process (for Codex, the native `codex app-server` started by the Node `codex` launcher), and everything that process started — tracked by the existing per-conversation owner registry, so that killing a pane leaves no agent process behind and releases the conversation lock before the kill is reported done, killing and immediately reopening a Codex conversation never produces "This conversation is open in another app", every way back into a conversation goes through that registry, and all eighteen defects in the agreed design are fixed: (1) "free" is published before Codex exits; (2) the launcher is force-killed first, orphaning the app-server; (3) sidecar stops run through one shared queue; (4) entry points back into a conversation don't wait for the old Codex to exit; (5) Shift-X skips panes that are still starting; (6) "terminal not found" counts as a successful kill; (7) the sidecar record tracks only one conversation id and isn't updated on fork; (8) another device can re-create a killed conversation; (9) a server restart or crash mid-stop leaves the record "active" and offers a dying app-server for reuse, and a Shift-X racing a graceful shutdown becomes "keep for reuse"; (10) MCP/CLI kill-tab and kill-pane only close, and respawn-pane leaves the old terminal running; (11) the Codex activity tracker ignores helper threads; (12) on macOS and Windows the sidecar is orphaned on every close; (13) other coding-agent panes (for example Claude Code, whose shell commands run in separate sessions) leak processes the same way; (14) three inconsistent idle-cleanup rules; (15) app-server death is only logged; (16) no stop logging and log retention of only about 12 hours; (17) unrealistic test fakes and Codex browser specs skipped on the cloud runner; (18) missing README coverage and accessibility gaps.

### Explicit constraints
- Use the existing owner registry in `crates/freshell-ownership` (Live / Stopping / Vacant) as the unit's Running / Stopping / Gone states; do not build a second state machine.
- Gone means the screen and the agent main process are confirmed dead and the conversation lock is released; it does not wait for every descendant. Leftover descendants are force-killed right after Gone and any survivors are logged.
- `terminal.exit`, `terminals.changed`, and Vacant are published only at Gone.
- Stopping is saved in the persisted record before any signal is sent; on server boot a Stopping unit has its stop finished and is never offered for reuse.
- The sidecar record tracks every thread its app-server holds (root, helper agents, forks, earlier conversations opened in that pane), found from the OS lock table or by asking the app-server which threads it has loaded.
- Each unit is stopped independently, not through one shared stop queue.
- Shift-X ("kill it now"; kill-then-immediately-reopen is a core workflow): send SIGINT to the agent main process, SIGKILL whatever is left (including the launcher) after 1 second, then kill all remaining descendants — including jobs the agent deliberately detached (dev servers, `nohup`, `setsid`) — found through OS containment, not a process-tree walk.
- Shift-X acknowledges only at Gone, and the tab closes only after that acknowledgement.
- Shift-X also applies to panes that are still starting, and cancels the start.
- "Not found" counts as kill success only when the registry confirms Gone; a second kill waits for the first; Shift-X on a unit that is already Stopping escalates straight to force.
- If Gone is not confirmed within 5 seconds, the tab stays open showing "Stopping…" until it is confirmed.
- A plain close (no Shift) leaves the unit running; reopening (Shift+Alt+T or the sidebar) reattaches to it; reopening never kills.
- Replace the hidden 24-hour agent-pane cap and the one-time 30-minute post-boot sweep with one rule based on real idleness, keeping 24 hours for agent panes. Plain shell panes and extension CLI panes keep today's idle cleanup (the "Auto-kill idle (minutes)" setting, 15 minutes by default).
- Idle is determined by asking the agent directly: every loaded thread, including helper threads, idle across a quiet window, nothing queued, and no automatically continuing goal. A pane waiting for the user's approval or input is not idle and cleanup leaves it alone.
- Cleanup sends a polite stop; if the unit is not Gone within a few seconds it is force-killed and a warning is logged. There is no "finishing up" waiting screen and no one-hour backstop.
- Every way back into a conversation goes through the registry and waits for Gone: auto-resume, the "Agent appears stuck" Restart, the exit banner's Relaunch/Reopen, a sidebar click, the Resume dialog, switching a pane between terminal Codex and freshcodex, MCP `respawn-pane`, and other devices.
- If the conversation is already held by a live Freshell pane, as its main conversation or as an extra thread, reopening jumps to that pane with no prompt and no new UI.
- If the conversation is held by something outside Freshell (a shell `codex`, Codex's own daemon or desktop app, `codex exec`), Freshell does not wait forever and reports who holds it (process id and command).
- An app-server that dies mid-reply is a crash: bell, highlight, and auto-resume as today, with auto-resume waiting for Gone. App-server death must be detected, not only logged.
- If only the screen crashes and the agent is fine, start a new screen and reattach it to the running agent.
- If the agent exits on its own, the whole unit ends and nothing is left behind.
- A kill on one device shows the pane as plain "Stopped" on other devices using the existing stopped presentation, with no new wording and no automatic re-create; killed units are remembered so late-arriving or offline devices show Stopped instead of re-creating the conversation.
- Running sidecars still survive a server restart and are reclaimed as today; Stopping units stay Stopping across a restart and their stop is finished on boot; a kill always beats the keep-on-restart rule.
- MCP/CLI `kill-tab` and `kill-pane` behave like Shift-X; add separate close commands for detaching; `respawn-pane` goes through the registry.
- Contain each coding-agent pane's whole process set with the OS: a cgroup per pane on Linux, a Job Object per pane on Windows, and the best available equivalent on macOS. The Windows desktop app and macOS are in scope.
- Containment is built once, generically, for every coding-agent pane (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Kimi, and the rest); Codex is done first.
- Keep new UI minimal: add only a sidebar marker for agents running in the background and stopping, a right-click "Close and stop agent" on tabs and panes as the keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible equivalent of Shift-X, and a screen-reader label on the tab X; "Stopping…" appears in the tab only in the rare unconfirmed case; invent no other UI.
- Shift-X and cleanup stops are silent; restarted panes must not produce a "went idle" or "turn complete" highlight; a crash mid-reply still rings as today and is never routed through the silent kill path.
- Structured JSONL logging with severity, keyed by conversation, terminal, and owner: stop requested (reason; graceful or force), signal sent, Gone (duration, lock released), escalation (warn), unconfirmed (error), time spent waiting before a start, and an error whenever "already has an active writer" / "open in another app" occurs. Fix log retention to cover at least the cleanup window and reduce the HTTP request-line noise.
- Remove overbuilding: once containment and confirmed kills are in place, remove owner-registry blocking machinery that exists only because Freshell could not confirm a process died (for example "platform-limited" fences and buttons like "Force clear the platform-limited fence"). Build no plug-in framework for other providers' login restarts.
- README covers Shift+click and the right-click equivalent to kill, that a plain close keeps the agent running and reopen reattaches, and how to stop a background agent; update `docs/index.html` only for the sidebar marker, if it is significant.
- Tests: realistic fakes (a Node launcher in front of a separate main process; SIGTERM finishes the reply before exiting; SIGINT stops at once; a helper in its own process group and a shell command in its own session; a detached job; the flock-based "already has an active writer" refusal); Rust integration tests for Shift-X mid-turn, kill during start, double kill, kill vs auto-resume race, restart during Stopping, fork then restart and restore, extra-thread holder reopen, outside holder reported, unconfirmed kill keeps the record and logs an error, one test per entry point including `kill-pane`/`kill-tab`/`respawn-pane`, cleanup idleness (helpers, queued messages, goals; waiting-on-approval not idle), and sidecars still surviving a server restart; client unit tests (not-found is not success, Shift-X targets starting panes, other devices show Stopped and don't re-create, kills and restarts stay silent); browser e2e (kill mid-turn then immediate reopen with no "open in another app", plain close then reopen reattaches, right-click "Close and stop agent", sidebar marker) passing on the configured cloud e2e backend, with the "Requires codex binary" cloud skip removed for fake-based specs; an opt-in real-Codex contract test that SIGINT/SIGKILL releases the lock and resume works; and a Windows desktop app smoke test that kill-then-reopen works.
- Do not restart, signal, or modify Codex's own managed daemon (`codex app-server --managed-daemon`).
- No polling: new waiting and detection use OS or process events, not periodic checks.
- Never restart the live self-hosted Freshell server on port 3001 without the user's explicit "APPROVED"; do not kill or signal processes this work did not start, and verify process ids first.
- Never copy `~/.codex/auth.json` and never log tokens.
- Work in a dedicated `.worktrees/<slug>` worktree; never dirty `main`; use pnpm; do not create a PR or merge without the user's explicit approval.

### Accepted tradeoffs and residuals
- Shift-X is forceful: a turn killed by SIGKILL may show as "interrupted" when the conversation is resumed.
- Gone does not wait for every descendant; descendants that survive the follow-up kill are only logged.
- Freshell does not restart or repair Codex's own managed daemon after a login switch; that is left to upstream (openai/codex#22419).
- Automatic restart of Codex panes when the Codex login changes is deferred to a separate later build that reuses this work's registry and kill paths.
- A comment on openai/codex#22419 is deferred and will not be posted until the user approves its text.

**Goal:** Every coding-agent pane becomes one OS-contained unit whose Running / Stopping / Gone state is the owner registry's Live / Stopping / Vacant, so Shift-X (and every other stop) confirms the agent and its conversation lock are gone before anything reports success, every path back into a conversation waits for that, nothing the pane started is left running, and a server restart touches only the units that server itself recorded.

**Architecture:** A new leaf crate `freshell-containment` gives every coding-agent pane a contained process set (a systemd transient scope slice per pane on Linux, under a per-server slice; a Job Object per pane on Windows, plus, for WSL-mode panes, a systemd scope slice inside the distro when it runs a user manager, else a Perl child-subreaper reaper there; on Linux hosts without a user systemd manager, process trees rooted at a per-member child-subreaper shim, so every orphaned descendant stays in its pane's tree whatever it does to its environment; on macOS the tagged set plus the kernel's responsible-process membership, or fork tracking where that is unusable), an event-driven per-process exit watch (`ProcWatch`: pidfd / kqueue / process handle), one stop sequence (persist Stopping → SIGINT main → 1 s → kill the whole unit and its pinned roots → confirm screen and main dead and no member holding a conversation lock → sweep and log survivors), confirmed placement of every member, OS lock-holder lookups by file descriptor and listening-socket lookups over the unit's own members, and one persisted record per unit in the server's state directory (its pinned roots, conversation keys and Running/Stopping state). Boot reclaims or finishes exactly the units in those records, verifying every process by pid and start time before any signal. The owner registry stays the only state machine: it gains event-driven waiting (wakers, no polling), unit-scoped stop/commit over every key a unit owns, main/extra holds and a boot seed for persisted Stopping units; the WebSocket layer gets one unit lifecycle module through which every stop passes, which owns kill, crash, screen-respawn and cleanup decisions, silences attention edges from the start of a requested stop, never blocks a connection loop on a wait, and publishes `terminal.exit` / `terminals.changed` / Vacant only at Gone; the Codex sidecar record (v2) keeps the unit id, the native main process, the app-server's real `codexHome` and every held thread. The client sends kills by terminal id or create-request id, acknowledges only at Gone, shows "Stopping…" (derived from server state) in the rare unconfirmed case, and shows the existing "stopped" presentation on other devices. The WebSocket protocol version goes to 11.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.96 (tokio 1.52, libc 0.2.186, windows-sys 0.59 for Windows only, tracing), systemd 255 user manager (`systemd-run --user --scope`, `systemctl --user`), cgroup v2 (`cgroup.kill`, `cgroup.events`, `cgroup.freeze`), Linux pidfd and `/proc` fd/fdinfo, macOS kqueue + libproc, Windows Job Objects / Restart Manager / IP Helper; React 18 + Redux Toolkit + Vitest; Playwright (cloud e2e backend); Node fakes in `test/fixtures/coding-cli/codex-app-server/`.

## Load-bearing assumptions (validated in Stage 2)

Stage 2 tested every load-bearing claim of the Stage 1 plan. The full record — 52 rows, each with its verdict, evidence and the plan change it caused — is the ledger `<logs_dir>/load-bearing-ledger.md`; per-claim evidence is in `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-finder.md` and `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V1.md` … `V14.md`. This plan already incorporates every resulting change; tasks mark each one `(Stage 2: LB-xx)`.

Outcome of the Stage 1 assumptions:
- **A1 — `systemd-run --user --scope` places and preserves the pid.** Verified (LB-03, V1), from both the service context and an SSH session scope: same pid, PTY session kept, no signal mask or `pkttyagent` side effects, placement in tens of milliseconds (about 200 ms under a 50-start burst, V2). Scopes survive `systemctl --user restart`/`stop` of a `KillMode=control-group` service and screens exit on hangup (LB-04). Corrected parts: implicit slices are never garbage-collected, so every unit slice is stopped explicitly at Gone (LB-27); a wrapper failure exits 1 exactly like a crashed agent and a stalled bus hangs 90 s, so placement is confirmed and a failure is a typed start failure (LB-27, LB-16); scope names carry a per-boot nonce (LB-27); `--expand-environment=no` is passed (systemd 254+).
- **A2 — `cgroup.kill`, `cgroup.freeze`, `cgroup.events` on the user-manager slice.** Verified (LB-05, V2), with caveats the plan now follows: events can arrive up to about 10 ms late and coalesce, and are lost for a cgroup removed meanwhile, so waits watch only the unit slice, always with a deadline, and Gone never depends on a transient `populated 0`.
- **A3 — Evicting a managed-daemon process out of a pane slice with `busctl`.** Dropped as unnecessary (LB-49): a frozen slice's non-spared members are SIGKILLed by pidfd and the spared ones are thawed and logged (the premise was observed in V2).
- **A4 — pidfd semantics.** Established (kernel exit order; existing rust-gate tests). Cloud Run gen2 and the Docker sandbox support it (LB-07, V4; Cloud Run by Google's documentation), retired in practice by Task 2's start-up self-check log and an early cloud e2e run. Qualification (V4): a lock is released at the main process's exit only when no other live process shares its open file description, so the Gone lock check runs after the whole-unit kill.
- **A5 — Realistic fake lock via `flock(1)` on an inherited fd.** The tools exist everywhere, but the `/proc/locks` pid column names the acquirer (an exited `flock(1)`, or 0 inside another pid namespace), so holders are attributed by file descriptor instead (LB-28).
- **A6 — Codex 0.162 protocol shapes.** Confirmed with corrections (LB-38, LB-39, V9): helper spawn and resume emit no `thread/started` (new threads appear as `thread/status/changed` for an unseen id or in `collabAgentToolCall.receiverThreadIds`); helper busy/idle must come from status events; the TUI's ephemeral title threads answer `-32600` to queue and goal calls; only an `active` goal continues by itself; `thread/queue/list` cannot see messages queued in the TUI with Tab.
- **A7 — Windows placement.** Partly confirmed from documentation and source (LB-08, LB-10, V5); whether a Node-launched grandchild silently breaks away from a `BREAKAWAY_OK` unit job (LB-09) and whether a `LockFileEx` lock is always released by the time the holder's handle is signalled (LB-11) cannot be settled without a Windows run, so Task 6 starts with those runner tests and states both design branches and the rule that picks one. Nested child jobs' `ACTIVE_PROCESS_ZERO` messages arrive under the unit's key; the shim needs a console control handler; processes a WSL-mode pane starts inside the distro are outside any Job Object, so they run in a systemd scope slice inside the distro when it has a user manager, else under a Perl child-subreaper reaper, else only tagged, and are killed by a one-shot in-distro call made before Gone (LB-15; plan review R2-F1, R3-F1, R3-F3).
- **A8 — macOS degraded backend.** `NOTE_EXIT` works for non-children and the kernel releases a `flock` before posting it (LB-11, LB-12, V6), but a late registration or a non-zombie-aware lookup can report "exited" before the lock is released, `lsof` is replaced by libproc on the unit's members, and hardened binaries with `CS_RESTRICT` hide their environment (tag unreadable), so Task 7 starts with V6's tests T1–T4.
- **A9 — CI user manager.** Dropped (LB-50): CI proves the degraded backend; garageserver proves the systemd backend.
- **A10 — Real Codex thread lock without auth.** Partly false (LB-41, V8): an unauthenticated isolated home starts threads and the native holds the lock from `thread/start`, but a turnless thread cannot be resumed (`no rollout found`); a model-free `thread/shellCommand` materializes it. Corollary: a conversation killed before its first turn is started new by every entry point.
- **A11 — The 13-second hold was an extra-thread hold.** Not decision-controlling; covered by waiting for Gone, jump-to-holder, the outside-holder report and the writer-conflict ERROR log.

Assumptions the Stage 1 plan made implicitly and Stage 2 found false (each now fixed in the tasks): boot sweeps killed other servers' units and unverified pids (LB-01, LB-02 → per-server unit records, verified roots); Codex's daemon family includes a sibling updater without `--managed-daemon` (LB-06); managed-runtime panes still needed routing fixes (LB-13); several registry, start, crash, screen, wait, retry, shutdown, logging and evidence assumptions (LB-14 to LB-48). Open residual still to be settled by first use: the REST dispatch's `return_run_details=true` answer with the installed gh 2.45 (the fallback in Global Constraints covers it).

## Decisions (made here, within the User Request)

1. **Reopen of a conversation held as an extra thread (coordinator note 1, design §8.1).** Reopening jumps to the live pane whose unit holds the thread, even when that pane displays a different conversation; no prompt, no new UI, and nothing is released or killed. Rationale: the User Request says reopening jumps to the holding pane "as its main conversation or as an extra thread" with no prompt and no new UI, and that reopening never kills; releasing an idle extra in place would need Codex to unload it (≈60 s after `thread/unsubscribe`, design fact 3.5), which either stalls the reopen or requires killing the holder. If the holder unit has no pane on this device (it was plain-closed), the reopening pane attaches to the holder's terminal (the normal reattach). The registry records each hold as `HoldKind::Main` or `HoldKind::Extra`, so a handoff "switch" or reopen on an extra-held thread never stops the holder's unit (Stage 2: LB-25). Tested in Task 14 (server answer) and Task 27 (client jump).
2. **Signalling the native process (design §8.2).** Freshell keeps spawning `CODEX_CMD` (users run wrappers such as `~/.local/bin/codex` → `node …/codex.js`, or `codex.cmd` on Windows), discovers the native app-server as the member of the pane's own unit that owns the app-server's listening socket, and signals it directly through its pidfd/handle. It never relies on `codex.js` forwarding (which forwards only the first signal and orphans the native on SIGKILL). Escalation kills the whole unit, which includes the launcher. If no member of the unit owns the listener after the readiness probe (another pane's app-server answered on a reused port, or a wrapper moved the native out of reach), the start attempt fails, its unit is stopped and the start retries on a new port; there is no "launcher as main" fallback for Codex (Stage 2: LB-30).
3. **`kill_verified_sidecar_tree` (design §8.3).** Replaced, not reused: reattached sidecars are stopped through their reopened containment unit; the tree walk, its 50 ms polling loops and the `/proc` tag reaper (`reap_owned_codex_sidecars`) are deleted (the tag scan survives only as the degraded backend's member finder for a recorded unit id, generalized to `FRESHELL_UNIT_ID` plus the legacy `FRESHELL_CODEX_SIDECAR_ID` for v1 records).
4. **macOS containment (design §8.4).** Environment tag `FRESHELL_UNIT_ID` + process-tree enumeration (libproc) + a kernel-tracked membership that survives reparenting to launchd and a withheld environment (plan review R1-F2): the "responsible process" the kernel copies to every descendant at fork (each unit root is started through the `__unit-exec` shim as its own responsible process), or, when Task 7's first runner test shows that unusable, kqueue fork tracking (`NOTE_FORK` on every member), which covers by design only a process whose parent, process group or session is already tracked when the tracker handles the fork (its residual is stated in Task 7, and its test asserts unconditionally only what it guarantees; plan review R2-F2). Nothing stronger is open to an unprivileged, unentitled process on macOS: kqueue's follow-across-fork option `NOTE_TRACK` is refused with `ENOTSUP` (XNU `bsd/kern/kern_event.c` `filt_procattach`; `bsd/sys/event.h`: "no longer supported as of 10.5"; `<logs_dir>/scratch/macos-note-track.txt`), and Endpoint Security needs Apple's restricted `com.apple.developer.endpoint-security.client` entitlement and root, so that race is the platform's limit, listed with the residuals (plan review R3-F4) — then a stop-the-world `SIGSTOP` sweep and `SIGKILL`, with kqueue `NOTE_EXIT` for confirmed exit. Reported as the `macos-tag` backend (degraded: no `wait_empty`, same Gone semantics). An exit is concluded only from a `NOTE_EXIT` registered before the exit began or a zombie-aware lookup; lock holders and the listener come from libproc on the unit's members (no `lsof`); a target whose environment the kernel withholds (`CS_RESTRICT`) is reported as "environment withheld" and is found through the kernel-tracked membership, pinned roots and descendants; units are not retained across a restart on macOS, as today (base retains sidecars only on Linux, `crates/freshell-codex/src/launch_lifecycle.rs:1203`) (Stage 2: LB-11, LB-12, LB-26).
5. **Managed runtime (design §8.5).** Managed-runtime panes (shell and OpenCode in Docker souls) are already contained by their container and keep `managed_stop`, whose acknowledgement, exit and Vacant publication already come after a verified stop; production Codex panes are not managed (`managed_enabled: false`). The routing around them is fixed instead (Stage 2: LB-13): Shift-X cancels a starting managed pane through the supervisor by its createRequestId; kill-by-unknown-terminal consults the managed inventory; the stopped-pane record and the reconcile `stopped` verdict cover managed panes; automation routes managed panes to `managed_stop`; a failed managed stop is aborted back to Live; "Stopping…" covers managed panes; a managed agent (OpenCode) that exits cleanly on its own ends its unit, while a non-zero exit keeps today's supervisor recovery. Session-host Codex launches plan without a unit and keep their non-unit path (Stage 2: LB-43). No supervisor or session-host change beyond those.
6. **Plain shell and extension CLI panes keep today's idle cleanup; the single cleanup rule covers the agent panes (User Request).** The single rule: a pane with no attached viewer that has been really idle for 24 hours is politely stopped, and "really idle" is asked from the agent. A provider Freshell cannot ask counts as not idle (Stage 2: LB-42). The rule covers exactly the agent modes base treats as agent panes (`crates/freshell-terminal/src/registry.rs:2029-2033`, `is_agent_mode`: claude, codex, opencode, amplifier, gemini, kimi), and each of them can be asked: Amplifier through the session-log tracker Freshell already runs, Gemini and Kimi through per-pane lifecycle hooks (Decision 25, which Task 22 first checks against the real CLIs). Managed (supervisor-owned) rows stay outside the rule, as today (Stage 2: LB-43). Plain shell panes (`mode: "shell"`) and extension CLI panes stay outside it too. An extension CLI pane is a terminal pane whose mode is any other CLI: a `category: "cli"` extension manifest (for example one the user put under `~/.freshell/extensions/`) whose name is not one of the six agent modes (`crates/freshell-server/src/extensions.rs:197-221`, `:375-386`). Both keep exactly today's cleanup: the "Auto-kill idle (minutes)" setting (`settings.safety.autoKillIdleMinutes`, 15 by default) stays, with its settings plumbing and its slider, and today's reaper (`enforce_idle_kills`, `registry.rs:2068-2135`, run every 30 s by `spawn_idle_monitor`) keeps stopping a non-managed shell or extension CLI pane with no attached viewer whose meaningful activity is older than the setting when the client released it (or never referenced it), or older than 24 hours when only its connection dropped (`registry.rs:2081-2116`; both take the same branch today, `:2109-2116`, because neither is an agent mode). The one-time 30-minute post-boot sweep never touched either (it acts only on held Codex sidecar records, `crates/freshell-codex/src/sidecar_sweep.rs:172-198`), so removing it changes nothing for them. Task 22 makes the reaper skip agent-mode rows and the rule take only agent-mode rows, so the same test splits the rows and no row is judged by both rules. Plain shells are never units and keep today's kill. Extension CLI panes become units in Task 23, so from then on the reaper hands an idle extension CLI row to the cleanup driver, which stops it through its unit with the same polite cleanup stop as an agent unit: the pane is announced closed only once it is confirmed dead, and other devices are told it was stopped.
7. **`docs/index.html` (coordinator note 6).** Only the sidebar marker is added (it is a new, always-visible sidebar element, so it is significant). The mock's "Auto-kill idle (minutes)" slider row stays as it is, because the setting stays for plain shells and extension CLI panes (Decision 6).
8. **REST/MCP/CLI kill when Gone is not confirmed within 5 s (coordinator note 6).** `POST /api/panes/{id}/kill` and `POST /api/tabs/{id}/kill` wait up to 5 s: on Gone they close the pane/tab and answer `200 {"ok":true,"status":"stopped"}`; otherwise they answer `202 {"ok":false,"status":"stopping"}`, leave the tab open (clients show "Stopping…"), and close it automatically when Gone is confirmed. The same 5 s bound applies to every REST/MCP route that waits for Gone (`respawn-pane` included). An unknown pane id answers 404. MCP/CLI print the status (Stage 2: LB-20, LB-24).
9. **`respawn-pane` when the conversation is already held (coordinator note 6; plan review R1-F7).** `respawn-pane` is agent-driven, and agent-driven operations are focus-neutral by the repo's contract (AGENTS.md: they never move the user's selection; focus moves only through the explicit select verbs). So the automation form of "reopening jumps to the holding pane" is a success answer that names the holder, which the caller selects with `select-pane` if it wants focus there; moving the user's focus from an automation verb would break that contract, so the route never does (plan review R3-F5). Every live Freshell holder gets the same kind of answer, whatever its pane kind (plan review R3-F5). The route first checks the holder: (a) a different live pane holds the conversation — a terminal pane whose unit holds it, or a fresh-agent pane whose session holds it, as its main conversation or as an extra thread → nothing is stopped, spawned or focused (reopening never kills) and the answer is `200 {"ok":true,"status":"open-in-pane","paneId":<holder pane>,"terminalId":<holder terminal, present only for a terminal holder>,"message":"conversation <id> is already open in pane <paneId>; select-pane <paneId> switches to it"}`, which MCP and the CLI pass through as their result; (b) a live Freshell holder that no pane shows (a plain-closed background agent: a terminal unit or a fresh-agent session) → the route stops the target pane's own unit and attaches the pane to the holder (a terminal holder's terminal, or a fresh-agent session's own pane content), the normal reattach, as Decision 1's reopen does, answering as a respawn does; (c) only a holder outside Freshell keeps a refusal: Task 16's 409 `CONVERSATION_HELD_ELSEWHERE` naming the process by pid and name. A claim refused inside `spawn_terminal_pane` because another Freshell pane claimed the conversation after the check goes back to the holder check once and answers from it. The earlier 409 `RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` for a fresh-agent holder is withdrawn, because it made the answer depend on the holder's pane kind; Task 20 updates `mcp-bridge-rust.spec.ts:540-575`, which pinned it. With no holder it stops the target pane's own unit (waiting for Gone under the 5 s bound), then claims the conversation through the registry (Stage 2: LB-24).
10. **Killed-unit memory for late/offline devices.** A durable `StoppedPaneRecord` (pane ledger; one record per stop, which no later stop overwrites, found by its terminal id and by its create-request id; a fresh-agent stop's record is keyed by the create-request id bound to the conversation at that stop, or by the conversation alone when none is bound, so stopping a reopened conversation again never replaces the record of an earlier stop and every create-request id the conversation had at a stop stays remembered, plan review R2-F3; kept with no expiry, plan review R1-F5: the User Request sets no time limit and a record is a few hundred bytes) is written at Gone of every requested stop and of every clean self-exit, from the unit path and the managed kill path alike; a failed write is logged. Attach to an unknown terminal answers `INVALID_TERMINAL_ID` with `terminalStopped: true`; reconcile answers the new verdict `stopped`; a create carrying a killed create-request id is answered as stopped; all fold to the existing "session was stopped — reopen it to resume this conversation" bar. Reopen from that bar mints a new create-request id, so the record is never consumed by a stale device. A device that comes back after any length of time is still answered "stopped" (Stage 2: LB-36, LB-13, LB-42).
11. **Windows soft interrupt.** Windows has no SIGINT for a console-less sidecar; Shift-X there writes Ctrl+C (ETX) into the unit's PTY screen when it has one, and otherwise proceeds straight to `TerminateJobObject` (logged as `signal: "none"`, `reason: "windows-no-console"`). The `__unit-exec` shim installs a console control handler that returns TRUE, so a Ctrl+C reaches the agent without ending the shim (Stage 2). Windows keeps today's rule that sidecars are not retained across a server restart (base detaches and records a sidecar only on Linux, `crates/freshell-codex/src/launch_lifecycle.rs:1203`; elsewhere it uses `kill_on_drop` and a shutdown teardown); `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` is new here and also ends a unit when the server dies without its graceful shutdown (for example the desktop app's `TerminateProcess`), which base leaks. WSL-mode panes (pane shell `wsl` or a Linux cwd) run their CLI inside the distro behind a `wsl.exe` relay that is the unit's main, its screen and its Job Object member; the processes inside the distro are out of any Job Object's reach, so they get Linux containment inside the distro, with no new shipped binary (Stage 2: LB-15; plan review R2-F1). The spawn spec runs `wsl.exe [-d <distro>] [--cd <dir>] --exec sh -c <WSL_UNIT_EXEC_SH> sh <unit id> <cli…>`: a short POSIX `sh` prelude, passed as one argument like the stop's scan script, that exports `FRESHELL_UNIT_ID=<unit id>` (part of the spec itself, independent of WSLENV), so every process the CLI starts inside the distro carries the unit tag, and then runs the CLI under the strongest containment the distro offers, in the same order as on a Linux host (plan review R3-F3): (1) when the distro runs systemd with a user manager the prelude can reach (one bounded probe), it execs the CLI in place through `systemd-run --user --scope` in the slice `freshell-wsl-<unit id>.slice`: a real cgroup per pane inside the distro, which keeps every detached job whatever it does to its environment (the user-bus address `systemd-run` needs is set for `systemd-run` alone and never reaches the CLI); (2) otherwise, when `perl` is on `PATH` (`perl-base` is an Essential, required package on Debian and Ubuntu, the WSL default, so every Debian-family distro has it), it execs the in-distro reaper `WSL_REAPER_PL`, a port of Task 4's `--reaper` shim that uses only `perl-base`: it becomes a child subreaper, runs the CLI as its child in the CLI's own process group made the terminal's foreground group (a Ctrl+C reaches the CLI, never the reaper), forwards SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT, reaps every child, and when the CLI ends kills what is left of its tree (sparing the Codex daemon family) and exits with the CLI's status, so a detached job stays in the reaper's tree whatever it does to its environment, and no zombie is left for the CLI to collect (checked on this host before the change, `<logs_dir>/scratch/subreaper/run-perl.txt`: an env-cleared `setsid` job was reparented to the reaper; Ctrl+C reached only the agent; after a SIGINT, a PTY hangup or an outside SIGKILL of the agent, the reaper killed the detached and `nohup` jobs and exited only after the agent was dead); (3) otherwise it execs the CLI directly, tagged. Stopping (plan review R3-F1): Gone for such a unit means its CLI inside the distro is confirmed dead, not only the relay. Shift-X writes Ctrl+C into the PTY (above); when the relay has not exited by the escalation, the backend first makes ONE bounded, one-shot `wsl.exe [-d <distro>] --exec sh -c <WSL_TAG_SCAN_SH> sh <unit id>` call, before it terminates anything: the slice tier freezes the unit's slice, SIGKILLs every member except the Codex daemon family (judged per process by its own argv, plus its descendants), thaws it and stops the slice; the reaper tier SIGSTOPs then SIGKILLs every descendant of the unit's reaper, sparing the daemon family and never signalling the reaper itself; the tag tier then does the same to every remaining process whose environment holds exactly that tag, sparing the daemon family and the reaper; it reports the tier it used and what it killed, spared and failed to kill, by pid and process name only. Then the backend terminates the job's other members by handle and leaves the relay alone: `wsl.exe --exec` exits only after the process it started inside the distro has exited (the CLI itself, or the reaper once it has reaped the CLI), so the relay's own exit is the event that confirms the CLI's death, and it is the unit's Gone (new assumption, checked by Task 34's DANDESKTOP WSL case). A relay that has not exited goes down the ordinary unconfirmed path (ERROR `unit.stop.unconfirmed` 5 s after the final signal, the record stays Stopping, the tab shows "Stopping…"), and the next Force request repeats the in-distro call. A WSL unit's record carries its distro, so a Stopping record finished at boot (its relay already gone) makes the same call twice, once to kill and once, after the first returns, to confirm that no process of the unit is left alive, before its Gone; a second call that still finds one leaves the record Stopping with the same ERROR. Limit, stated honestly: only in a distro with neither a reachable user manager nor `perl` (for example a minimal Alpine) does the tag alone find members, so a detached process that clears its own environment can escape there; otherwise nothing the CLI starts inside the distro escapes except what another service starts on its behalf. A Codex pane in WSL mode gets the same treatment for its distro-side TUI, while its app-server and everything it starts are Windows processes in the Job Object.
12. **`kill_all` timing.** The 1 s is the maximum grace for the main process after SIGINT; the rest of the unit (and its pinned roots, directly) is killed as soon as the main process exits or the second elapses, whichever is first (no idle waiting once the main process is gone).
13. **Codex TUI exits.** The Codex TUI never exits when its app-server dies or its remote drops (it reconnects for up to 120 s and then stays open), so app-server death is detected from the native main process's own exit event and ends the whole unit under the crash rules (Stage 2: LB-40). A screen exit with code 0 while the app-server lives and no turn is running on any loaded thread is the user quitting Codex: the whole unit ends (in remote mode `/quit` only detaches, so the app-server is stopped explicitly). Exit 0 while a turn is still running (Codex's "quit, run in background") and any non-zero or signal exit with the app-server alive are screen-only exits: the screen is restarted in the same terminal row (same terminal id, continuing its output sequence) against the running app-server; only crashes count toward the existing respawn liveness window. During server shutdown a killed screen takes the retention path, never a restart.
14. **Fresh-agent pane X.** A plain pane-header X on a fresh-agent pane now detaches (like every plain close); Shift+click on the pane X and the right-click item stop the agent. This makes "plain close leaves the unit running" true for every pane type. Consequently background fresh-agent sessions get the sidebar marker, the single cleanup rule and the stopped-on-other-devices memory, like terminal panes (Stage 2: LB-42).
15. **freshopencode: one daemon per pane (plan review R1-F4).** Today every freshopencode pane shares one `opencode serve` daemon (`crates/freshell-freshagent/src/lib.rs:1959-1979`), so every tool or shell command any session runs is that shared daemon's child and no per-pane unit could contain it. Each freshopencode pane now gets its own daemon, started inside that pane's session unit as the unit's main: `FreshAgentState`'s single manager cell becomes a map from the pane's fresh-agent session to its own `OpencodeServeManager`, the shape the managed session host already uses with one daemon per soul (`crates/freshell-session-host/src/providers/fresh_agent.rs:1-5, 181-190`). All daemons keep sharing OpenCode's one database (`crates/freshell-opencode/src/serve.rs:2183`), so any pane's daemon can resume any `ses_*`. Shift-X, a kill command or cleanup first retires that pane's manager, so its respawn ladder cannot start another daemon, then stops the unit: the daemon and everything it started, detached jobs included, die by containment, and Gone is the daemon's confirmed exit. A plain close leaves the pane's daemon running (a background session, Decision 14). Daemon loss is per pane: `OPENCODE_DAEMON_LOST` reaches only that pane's session; the death ends the old unit as a crash (ringing as today when a turn was in flight), and the manager's existing backoff respawn starts the new daemon, in a fresh unit for the same session, only after the old unit's Gone; its revival pass then re-bridges that session as today. At shutdown every pane's daemon unit is stopped at once under Task 19's deadline. Cost, listed in the final report: each freshopencode pane pays OpenCode's own server start (the existing health budget) at its first use instead of once per server, and runs its own daemon process. Terminal-mode OpenCode panes are ordinary per-pane units.
16. **Retention (plan review R2-F4).** Successful HTTP request lines move to DEBUG (96.6% of today's volume), and the server's log rotation keeps by age instead of by count alone, because a count of size-limited files holds the cleanup window only at an assumed volume: a burst of WARN 4xx lines could rotate three 10 MiB files within hours. A rotated file is deleted only once its newest line is older than the 24-hour cleanup window (its modification time: a rotated file is never written again), and the two most recent backups are kept whatever their age, as today. A disk-safety cap on the total size of the server's log files (1 GiB by default, about 590 times the measured peak non-HTTP day of about 1.8 MB, `plan-automation-activity-logging.md` §4.2) is the only thing that can delete a file younger than the window; when it does, the server logs ERROR `log.retention.cap_forced_delete` with the deleted file's age, so retention never silently falls below the window. Tests prove the time property directly, with file ages set by the test, at volumes far beyond what the old count bound held, instead of at an assumed volume; the two existing rotation tests that assert a bounded file count run with a zero window, which keeps today's count bound (Stage 2: LB-48).
17. **Sidebar "stopping" signal.** A live `session.runtimeOwner{transition:"stopping"}` frame is broadcast when a stop begins (it is not one of the Gone-only publications); the sidebar marker and the reconnect replay both use the owner record, so no new list endpoint field is needed. A Stopping owner record never renders the "This conversation is being reopened elsewhere…" card (Stage 2: LB-37).
18. **Realistic fake's lock.** The fake native takes a real `flock(2)` on its own open file description through util-linux `flock -x -n` on an inherited fd (A5) instead of a Rust or Python helper: it keeps all of the existing Node fake's protocol behaviors in one process, and the lock lives and dies with the native exactly like Codex's `O_CLOEXEC` `File::try_lock`. Freshell attributes lock holders by file descriptor (`/proc/<pid>/fd` + `fdinfo` `lock:` lines), never by the `/proc/locks` pid column (which names the exited `flock(1)`, or 0 inside a pid namespace), so the fake's long-lived native is found as the holder (Stage 2: LB-28). On Windows the fake native keeps a small compiled helper holding a real `LockFileEx` lock (Stage 2: LB-11). Outside-holder tests use `flock -x <file> <cmd>`, whose holder (by fd) is `<cmd>`.
19. **Linux backends.** Two only: systemd transient scopes (full: a cgroup per pane, kernel-tracked) and, where the host gives no way to create a cgroup, the fallback reported as `linux-tag` (degraded only in having no emptiness event). The rule, stated plainly (plan review R3-F2): every pane gets its own cgroup wherever Linux lets the server have one, which for an unprivileged server is exactly where a systemd user manager answers — the user's hosts (garageserver, a WSL distro with systemd, a server started from SSH or from `launch-rust.sh`) all do; the fallback runs only where no cgroup can be had. Linux delegates cgroups to an unprivileged user only through that user's manager: on this host, uid 1000 can create a cgroup only inside `user@1000.service`, cannot create one in its own session scope or in `user-1000.slice` (root-owned), and cannot move even its own shell from the session scope into the delegated subtree (the kernel requires write access to the common ancestor), so only the user manager, with the system manager's help, can place a process there; the Docker sandbox mounts cgroupfs read-only even for container root (`<logs_dir>/scratch/subreaper/cgroup-probe.txt`), and Cloud Run gives containers no write access to `/sys` and runs the e2e image as `USER node` with privilege escalation disabled (`<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V4.md` §3). No raw-cgroupfs backend is built: no supported host offers a writable delegated cgroup without also offering a user manager, so it would be unused code. The systemd backend's suites are run where cgroups exist, on garageserver with `FRESHELL_REQUIRE_SYSTEMD_CONTAINMENT=1` (Tasks 4, 5, 23, 34), which fails them if the systemd backend is not selected. The fallback's membership is kept by the kernel too, through `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` (plan review R2-F1): every member it spawns starts through the `__unit-exec --reaper` shim (Task 4), which marks itself a child subreaper, runs the command as its child in the command's own process group (made the terminal's foreground group when there is one, so a Ctrl+C typed into the pane reaches the agent and never the shim), forwards SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT to it, and, when the command exits, kills what is left of its tree (sparing the Codex daemon family) and exits with the command's status. The kernel reparents every orphaned descendant (a `setsid` or double-forked job, whatever it does to its environment) to its nearest living subreaper ancestor, so while the shim lives everything the pane started stays in the shim's tree, and that tree is the unit's membership; the environment tag stays a second finder (for a shim killed from outside Freshell, and for v1 records adopted without a shim). Checked on this host before the change (`<logs_dir>/scratch/subreaper/run1.txt`): under a PTY set up as portable-pty does it, a `setsid` job that cleared its environment after its parent exited was reparented to the shim; a Ctrl+C typed into the PTY reached only the agent; a SIGINT sent to the shim was forwarded, ended the agent, and the shim then killed the detached job and a `nohup` job and exited 0; a PTY hangup did the same and the shim died by SIGHUP. `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` also succeeds unprivileged inside the Docker sandbox image with `no-new-privileges` and the default seccomp profile (`<logs_dir>/scratch/subreaper/sandbox-prctl.txt`); anywhere it is refused, the shim exits 126 and the start fails loudly, never silently uncontained. Limits: a process another service starts on the agent's behalf (as on every backend), and, when the shim itself is killed from outside Freshell before the stop, an untagged detached process it held. CI runs this fallback (Stage 2: LB-50).
20. **Per-server unit records (Stage 2: LB-01, LB-02, LB-23, LB-26, LB-32).** Every unit is recorded in the server's own state directory before its first member starts (`<state_root>/units/<unit id>.json`: provider, terminal and create-request ids, conversation keys, pinned roots by pid and start time, Running/Stopping), and the record is deleted at Gone. Persisted Stopping lives in this record for every provider; the Codex sidecar record keeps only sidecar data. Boot reclaims (Codex sidecars) or finishes (everything else) exactly the units in the records it owns, seeding the registry Stopping for their conversations first, and signals only roots whose pid and start time still match; no slice, tag or process enumeration is used to find leftovers. Each record is locked by the server that wrote it for that server's lifetime, so two servers sharing a state directory (the live server and a worktree scratch server) both record their units and neither ever touches a record the other still holds; a booting server takes over only records whose server is gone (plan review R1-F1). No unit runs without a record: a state directory that cannot be created fails coding-agent starts with a typed error. systemd slices live under a slice named from the state root, so servers with different state roots never share a slice (servers sharing one share only that parent slice, which nothing enumerates). The server strips an inherited unit tag at start. Retention across a restart (Linux only) is decided per unit id from the sidecar record and the registry, not from a bound terminal.
21. **Confirmed placement and starts (Stage 2: LB-16, LB-17, LB-27).** Every stop also kills the unit's pinned roots directly, so a kill during placement cannot miss a process. A start is settled only when its members are bound and their placement is confirmed by a one-shot check (at the readiness probe, or at a 2 s deadline); a member that exits before confirmation or is unplaced at the deadline is a typed start failure with an ERROR log, never a crash or a screen restart. Each start attempt uses its own unit; a stopped unit accepts no new members. Killed create-request ids are remembered so a create or kill arriving later is answered correctly.
22. **One shutdown deadline (Stage 2: LB-45).** On SIGTERM the layout is flushed and retention records are written first; then every stop (terminal units, fresh-agent session units including each freshopencode pane's daemon unit, unadopted launch plans) starts at once and all are awaited under one 3.5 s deadline from signal receipt, well inside the 5 s hard-exit watchdog and `scripts/launch-rust.sh`'s 5 s stop poll. A stop cut off keeps its persisted Stopping record and is finished at the next boot.
23. **Never-materialized conversations start new (Stage 2: LB-41).** A conversation killed before its first turn has no rollout; every entry point that gets Codex's `no rollout found` answer (or a `resume` TUI's "No saved session found") starts a new conversation in that pane instead of reporting an error or restarting a screen.
24. **Silent stops (Stage 2: LB-37).** Every requested stop notifies the activity tracking for its terminal when the stop starts, so no idle, turn-complete or bell edge can be produced between the soft signal and Gone; a crash is never routed through that path and still rings.
25. **Asking Gemini and Kimi whether they are idle (plan review R1-F6).** Base has no status channel for either (`crates/freshell-ws/src/activity.rs:1151`, "status-inert"), so the single cleanup rule could never judge them. Both CLIs document lifecycle hooks (Gemini CLI: prompt submit, turn end and a tool-permission notification; Kimi Code CLI: `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop` and `Notification` with `permission_prompt`). Freshell adds hook entries to the per-pane launch configuration it already writes for these CLIs (`crates/freshell-platform/src/mcp_inject.rs:987-998`); each hook runs Freshell's own executable as `<exe> __agent-hook <prompt|stop|waiting>` (the same executable and hidden-subcommand mechanism as `__unit-exec`), which appends one line `{"event","at"}` to the file named by `FRESHELL_AGENT_STATUS_FILE` in the pane's environment. The server watches each such file with one file-change watch (event-driven, no polling) and keeps the latest event: `prompt` → busy, `waiting` → waiting on the user, `stop` → idle; before any event the answer is unknown. Idle therefore needs all three signals the hooks give at once (plan review R3-F6): a turn has ended (`stop`), no prompt was submitted after it, and no permission notification came after it. Neither CLI shows a queue to its hooks; input typed during a turn is submitted by the CLI when the turn ends, and that submission fires `prompt`, which the cleanup rule's quiet window sees as work. New assumption, checked first in Task 22 Step 1 against the installed CLIs: each CLI takes these hooks from per-pane configuration and fires them as described, including `prompt` for queued input it sends at a turn's end; a CLI that cannot is left unknown (never auto-stopped) and the final report raises that conflict with the single 24-hour rule to the user. Step 1 also checks whether a CLI keeps queued input unsent after the user interrupts a turn (as Codex's TUI does, V9 N7): if it does, its pane is idle only when its hooks can tell a normal turn end from an interrupted one (an interrupted end then counts as busy until the next `prompt`, Task 22's rule for Codex), and otherwise it stays unknown, as above.

## File map (responsibilities)

New crate `crates/freshell-containment/` (leaf: `libc`, `tokio`, `tracing`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `uuid`, `sha2` (Task 5, per-server namespace); `windows-sys` on Windows only):
- `Cargo.toml` — crate manifest; `[[bin]] freshell-unit-exec` (test shim binary, `src/bin/freshell-unit-exec.rs`); `[[bin]] freshell-test-helper` (Task 6: lock holder, idle and breakaway-daemon modes for the Windows decision tests).
- `src/lib.rs` — module wiring and re-exports.
- `src/unit_id.rs` — `UnitId` (dash-free `u` + 32 hex), `UNIT_ENV = "FRESHELL_UNIT_ID"`.
- `src/process.rs` — `ProcIdentity` (pid, start time, process name), `identity(pid)`, `name(pid)`, `is_codex_daemon_family(argv)`, `environ_read` (value / absent / withheld), per-OS process facts (start time, argv, environ, children).
- `src/startup.rs` — server-start prelude (Task 2): remove inherited unit tags, raise the open-file soft limit, the one-shot containment self-check log.
- `src/record.rs` — `UnitRecord`/`UnitRecordState` and the record store under `<state_root>/units/`, each record locked by the server that wrote it (Task 4): the only persisted unit state and the only way a restarted server finds units.
- `src/proc_watch.rs` — `ProcWatch` (event-driven exit + identity-pinned signals) per OS.
- `src/backend/mod.rs` — internal `Backend` trait, `BackendKind`, `Capability`.
- `src/backend/systemd.rs` — Linux systemd transient-scope backend (per-server slice, slice per unit stopped explicitly at Gone, per-boot scope names, `cgroup.kill`, `cgroup.events` on the slice with deadlines, `cgroup.freeze` + pidfd kill of non-spared members when the daemon family is present, placement confirmation, deadline-bounded probe).
- `src/backend/tag.rs` — Unix tag backend (Linux `/proc` and macOS `libproc`/`sysctl`), members pinned before the soft signal, stop-the-world sweep; on Linux every member spawned under the `--reaper` shim (Task 4); on macOS also the responsible-process membership (Task 7 Branch A). `src/backend/macos_forks.rs` exists only if Task 7 selects Branch B (the per-unit kqueue fork tracker).
- `src/backend/windows_job.rs` — Windows Job Object backend + completion port (zero messages re-checked against the job's active count; the branch chosen by Task 6's first runner tests).
- `src/backend/wsl_scan.rs` — WSL-mode panes: the in-distro exec prelude (systemd scope slice when the distro has a user manager, else the tag) and the one-shot in-distro slice-and-tag kill (POSIX `sh` scripts, their `wsl.exe` arguments and the output parser; Task 23).
- `src/reaper.rs` — Linux `__unit-exec --reaper`: the child-subreaper shim every Linux fallback member starts under (Task 4).
- `src/exec_shim.rs` — `unit_exec_main` (Windows self-placement; Linux `--reaper`, Task 4; macOS `--disclaim` in-place exec, Task 7; elsewhere a plain exec used only by tests) and `agent_hook_main` (`__agent-hook`, Task 22).
- `src/containment.rs` — `Containment` (backend selection, `create_unit`, `recorded_units`, `reopen_unit` from a record, `adopt_legacy` with pinned roots, global handle).
- `src/unit.rs` — `AgentUnit`, `MemberRole`, `Placement`, `StopRequest`, `StopMode`, `StopReason`, `StopHandle`, `StopReport`, the single stop sequence.
- `src/directory.rs` — `UnitDirectory` (unit id ↔ terminal id / create-request id, start cancellation and the killed-start memory, start settlement after confirmed placement, `entry_with_member`, the lifecycle hook).
- `src/locks.rs` — `LockHolder` (pid, name, path), `lock_holders(paths)` and `lock_holders_among(paths, pids)` by file descriptor, `codex_thread_lock_path`.
- `src/listener.rs` — `listening_socket_owner(port, unit members)`.
- `src/events.rs` — `UnitLogKeys` and every `freshell_unit` JSONL event.
- `src/testing.rs` — env-gated test hooks (`FRESHELL_TEST_HOOKS=1` + `FRESHELL_TEST_UNIT_GONE_DELAY_MS`, `FRESHELL_TEST_UNIT_PERSIST_DELAY_MS`).
- `tests/conformance.rs`, `tests/support/mod.rs` — backend conformance suite run against the selected backend and the tag backend.

Existing files (one responsibility each, listed by owning task):
- `crates/freshell-ownership/src/lib.rs` — waker-based `wait_settled`, `AlreadyStopping`, unit-scoped stop/commit, extra-thread holds, boot seed (Task 8); Fenced removal (Task 24).
- `crates/freshell-codex/src/sidecar_store.rs` — record v2 (unit id, native main, held threads, the sidecar's own `codexHome`; no stop state) (Task 9); `record_for_unit` (Task 19).
- `crates/freshell-codex/src/launch_lifecycle.rs` — sidecar spawned into the unit, main discovery, per-unit stop, retention vs kill (Task 10); held threads (Task 14).
- `crates/freshell-codex/src/sidecar_reconcile.rs`, `runtime_select.rs`, `transport.rs` — reattach through units, claim by any held thread (Tasks 9, 10, 19); `sidecar_sweep.rs` deleted (Task 22); tag reaper deleted (Task 23).
- `crates/freshell-codex/src/idle_probe.rs` (new) — direct Codex idleness query (Task 22).
- `crates/freshell-terminal/src/registry.rs` — unit rows, ending intent, `complete_unit_end`, `replace_screen`, screen-exit hook (Task 11), `respawn_spec` (Task 17), idle-rule reads and the idle reaper limited to plain shell and extension CLI rows (Task 22), which hands idle unit rows to the cleanup driver (Task 23).
- `crates/freshell-ws/src/unit_lifecycle.rs` (new) — the single stop path, kill/crash/respawn orchestration, Gone publishing and the live "stopping" frame (Tasks 12, 13, 17, 19, 29); `unit_threads.rs` (Task 14), `gone_wait.rs` (Task 15: parked, cancellable waits), `unit_holders.rs` (Task 16), `unit_cleanup.rs` (Task 22; its idle-unit hook, Task 23), `unit_stopper.rs` (Task 15, extended by Task 20).
- `crates/freshell-ws/src/terminal.rs` — create paths in units (Tasks 12, 23), kill handler (Task 13), holder answers (Tasks 14, 16), claim waits (Task 15), stopped attach answer (Task 18).
- `crates/freshell-ws/src/codex_proxy_route.rs` — held-thread feed (Task 14), writer-conflict detection (Task 16), richer loss logs (Task 17), work events (Task 22).

## Shared interfaces (defined once; later tasks use these exact names)

```rust
// crates/freshell-containment/src/unit_id.rs
pub const UNIT_ENV: &str = "FRESHELL_UNIT_ID";
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(transparent)]
pub struct UnitId(String);
impl UnitId {
    pub fn mint() -> Self;                    // "u" + uuid v4 simple (32 lowercase hex)
    pub fn parse(raw: &str) -> Option<Self>;  // accepts exactly that shape
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str;
}

// crates/freshell-containment/src/process.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ProcIdentity { pub pid: u32, pub start: u64, pub name: String } // name = process name, never argv (Stage 2: LB-46)
pub fn identity(pid: u32) -> std::io::Result<ProcIdentity>;
pub fn name(pid: u32) -> std::io::Result<String>;
pub fn is_codex_daemon_family(argv: &[String]) -> bool; // per process, own argv; spares only (Stage 2: LB-06, Global Constraints)

// crates/freshell-containment/src/proc_watch.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum Sig { Interrupt, Terminate, Kill }
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct ProcWatch { /* Arc<inner> */ }
impl ProcWatch {
    pub fn open(pid: u32) -> std::io::Result<Self>;                  // pins the current incarnation
    pub fn open_expecting(pid: u32, start: u64) -> std::io::Result<Self>; // ErrorKind::NotFound if start differs or pid gone
    pub fn identity(&self) -> &ProcIdentity;
    pub fn pid(&self) -> u32;
    pub fn has_exited(&self) -> bool;                                 // non-blocking
    pub async fn exited(&self) -> std::io::Result<()>;               // event-driven; never panics (Stage 2: LB-14)
    pub fn signal(&self, sig: Sig) -> std::io::Result<()>;            // never reaches a recycled pid
}

// crates/freshell-containment/src/backend/mod.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum BackendKind { SystemdScope, LinuxTag, WindowsJob, MacosTag }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct Capability { pub kind: BackendKind, pub full: bool, pub reason: Option<String> }

// crates/freshell-containment/src/containment.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)] pub struct SelectOptions { pub shim: Option<ShimCommand>, pub state_root: std::path::PathBuf } // empty root: in-memory records (tests only)
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct ShimCommand { pub exe: std::path::PathBuf, pub leading_args: Vec<String> }
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct Containment { /* Arc<dyn Backend> */ }
impl Containment {
    pub fn select(opts: SelectOptions) -> Self;          // logs event=containment.backend once
    pub fn tag_backend(opts: SelectOptions) -> Self;      // forced degraded backend (tests, sandbox)
    pub fn capability(&self) -> Capability;
    pub fn create_unit(&self, id: UnitId, label: UnitLabel) -> std::io::Result<AgentUnit>;
    pub fn recorded_units(&self) -> std::io::Result<Vec<UnitRecord>>;            // this server's own records only (Stage 2: LB-01)
    pub fn reopen_unit(&self, record: &UnitRecord, label: UnitLabel) -> std::io::Result<AgentUnit>; // roots re-pinned by (pid, start)
    pub fn adopt_legacy(&self, tag_key: &str, tag_value: &str, roots: &[(u32, u64)], label: UnitLabel) -> AgentUnit; // (pid, start) pairs (Stage 2: LB-02)
}
pub fn set_global_containment(c: Containment) -> bool;
pub fn global_containment() -> Option<Containment>;

// crates/freshell-containment/src/unit.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UnitLabel { pub provider: String, pub session_id: Option<String>, pub terminal_id: Option<String>,
                       pub mode: String, pub create_request_id: Option<String> }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum MemberRole { Screen, Agent }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Placement { pub wrapper: Option<Vec<String>>, pub env: Vec<(String, String)> }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum StopMode { Force, Graceful { grace: std::time::Duration } }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StopReason { ShiftX, KillCommand, Respawn, Cleanup, Handoff, StuckRestart, StartCancelled,
                      AgentExited { exit_code: Option<i64> }, PlacementFailed { exit_code: Option<i64> }, BootFinish, ServerShutdown }
pub type GoneCallback = Box<dyn FnOnce(StopReport) -> futures_core_shim::BoxFuture<'static, ()> + Send>;
pub struct StopRequest {
    pub mode: StopMode,
    pub reason: StopReason,
    pub initiator: String,
    pub operation_id: Option<String>,
    pub on_gone: Option<GoneCallback>,
    pub soft_interrupt: Option<Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StopReport { pub unit_id: UnitId, pub reason: String, pub mode: &'static str,
                        pub duration_ms: u64, pub escalated: bool, pub lock_released: bool }
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct StopHandle { /* tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<Option<StopReport>> */ }
impl StopHandle {
```

## Test command reference (from `workspace-baseline.md`; exact)

- Containment crate: `cargo test -p freshell-containment --locked`
- Containment on the degraded backend in the sandbox: `scripts/sandbox-test.sh "cargo test -p freshell-containment --locked"`
- Cross-target checks: `cargo check -p freshell-containment --tests --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked` and `cargo check -p freshell-containment --tests --target aarch64-apple-darwin --locked`
- Ownership: `cargo test -p freshell-ownership --locked`
- Codex (integration files need the feature): `cargo test -p freshell-codex --features real-transport --locked`
- Terminal: `cargo test -p freshell-terminal --locked`
- One ws integration file: `cargo test -p freshell-ws --test <file_stem> --locked`
- Server binary tests: `cargo build -p freshell-server --locked && FRESHELL_SERVER_BIN=$PWD/target/debug/freshell-server cargo test -p freshell-server --test <file_stem> --locked`
- Client unit tests: `pnpm run test:vitest run <paths...> --config config/vitest/vitest.config.ts`
- Cloud e2e (committed clean tree): `GCLOUD_ROBOT_REQUIRE=1 pnpm run test:e2e --project=chromium test/e2e-browser/specs/<spec>.spec.ts`
- Lint/types/format: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude freshell-tauri --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- Full gate: `GCLOUD_ROBOT_REQUIRE=1 FRESHELL_TEST_SUMMARY="codex-pane-lifecycle: <purpose>" pnpm run check`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing new (Node 22, `ws`, util-linux `flock`, `perl`; Rust std `File::try_lock` for the compiled lock holder).
- Produces (used by Tasks 6, 10, 12–23, 32, 34):
  - `node fake-codex-launcher.mjs <codex argv...>` — a launcher process that spawns `node fake-app-server.mjs <argv...>` as a separate native child with `FAKE_CODEX_ROLE=native`, forwards only the first SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and exits after the native (code, or 128+signal).
  - Native role behavior keys in `FAKE_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BEHAVIOR` (JSON): `turnCompleteDelayMs` (existing), `spawnHelperProcess` (bool, own process group, same session), `mcpChild` (bool, exits on stdin EOF), `turnSpawnsShellCommand` (bool, own session), `detachedJobOnTurn` (bool, reparented `nohup` job), `helperThreadOnTurn` (`{ "id": string, "durationMs": number, "closeAfterMs"?: number }`; `closeAfterMs`: the parent closes the helper at that time, Codex's `close_agent` (Stage 2: LB-38)), `preloadedThreads` (string[]: loaded and locked for the native's whole life, like conversations opened earlier in the pane), `queuedSubmissions` (`{ [threadId]: number }`), `goals` (`{ [threadId]: { "status": string } }`), `threadStartThreadId` (existing; when unset, each non-ephemeral `thread/start` in the native role gets a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` id instead of the shared `thread-new-1`, so two panes on one `CODEX_HOME` never collide on a real lock — finder §6 FA-9), `listenDelayMs` (number: the native waits this long before listening — makes "kill during start" reproducible), `ignoreSigint` (bool: record SIGINT but keep running — a wedged agent that only the whole-unit kill ends), `ignoreSigterm` (bool: record SIGTERM but never finish the polite stop), `approvalWaiting` (string[]: threads reported `active{waitingOnApproval}` by `thread/read`), `threadUnloadDelayMs` (number, default 60000 like Codex's `thread_unload_delay_secs`: how long a thread with no subscriber and no running turn stays loaded) (Stage 2: LB-38), `resumeNeedsRollout` (bool, default false: a cold `thread/resume` of an id that has no rollout file under `<CODEX_HOME>/sessions/` answers Codex's `{"code":-32600,"message":"no rollout found for thread id <id>"}` and takes no lock; opt-in because most later tests resume made-up ids) (Stage 2: LB-41; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V8.md` §41c).
  - Env: `FAKE_CODEX_MANIFEST_DIR` (launcher writes `launcher-<pid>.json`, native writes `native-<pid>.json`), `FAKE_UNIT_RECORD_DIR` (replaces `FAKE_CODEX_RECORD_DIR`: on every signal the native copies the `state` value of `<dir>/<FRESHELL_UNIT_ID>.json` — the per-unit record that is now the only place persisted Stopping lives — as compact JSON text into that signal's manifest entry, `null` when the variable or file is absent) (Stage 2: LB-32), `CODEX_HOME` (lock files under `<CODEX_HOME>/thread-writer-locks/`), `FAKE_CODEX_LOCK_HOLDER` (required off Linux: path of the compiled `fake-codex-lock-holder`; a native started off Linux without it exits 1 with `FAKE_CODEX_LOCK_HOLDER is required off Linux`, so the fake never silently holds no lock) (Stage 2: LB-11).
  - Native JSON-RPC (Codex 0.162 shapes, Stage 2: LB-38, LB-39; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V9.md` §38–39):
    - Locks: `thread/start`, a cold `thread/resume` and the fork child of `thread/fork` take a real exclusive lock per thread (Linux: an `flock` on the native's own open file description; off Linux: one compiled holder per thread) and answer `{"code":-32600,"message":"thread-store conflict: thread <id> already has an active writer"}` when another process holds it. A warm `thread/resume` of a thread this native already has loaded takes no lock and never conflicts (Codex's `resume_running_thread`). An ephemeral `thread/start {ephemeral: true}` takes no lock.
    - Announcements: `thread/started` is broadcast for `thread/start` (an ephemeral one carries `thread.ephemeral: true`) and for a fork child (with `forkedFromId`), never for a resume or a helper spawn. A cold resume broadcasts `thread/status/changed {notLoaded}` then `{idle}`. A helper spawn broadcasts `thread/status/changed {idle}` then `{active}` for the new id, plus `item/completed` on the root thread carrying `{type: "collabAgentToolCall", tool: "spawnAgent", receiverThreadIds: [<helper>]}`; the helper's `turn/started`/`turn/completed` go only to connections that were open when it spawned.
    - Subscriptions and unload: a thread's subscribers are the connection that started, resumed or forked it (for a helper: every connection open at its spawn); `thread/unsubscribe` or a closed connection removes one. A thread with no subscriber and no running turn unloads after `threadUnloadDelayMs`: its lock is released and the lock file deleted, it leaves `thread/loaded/list`, and `thread/status/changed {notLoaded}` then `thread/closed` are broadcast. A helper closed by its parent (`closeAfterMs`) ends a running turn as `interrupted` and broadcasts only `thread/status/changed {notLoaded}`. Preloaded threads never unload.
    - Queries: `thread/loaded/list` returns every loaded thread (ephemeral ones included) sorted by id, honouring `limit`/`cursor` with `nextCursor`; `thread/queue/list` and `thread/goal/get` answer from behavior, and for an ephemeral thread answer `{"code":-32600,"message":"ephemeral thread does not support queued submissions: <id>"}` / `"ephemeral thread does not support goals: <id>"`; `turn/interrupt` ends that thread's running turn as `interrupted`.
    - Turns: every `turn/start` gets a fresh turn id and the full lifecycle notifications (`thread/status/changed active` → `turn/started` → `thread/status/changed idle` → `turn/completed`) even without `recordTurns`; turns on an ephemeral thread complete after 50 ms and write no rollout.
    - Signals: SIGTERM drains (rejects new `turn/start` with `-32001 "app-server is draining"`, waits for running turns, exits 100 ms after the last); SIGINT ends running turns, reporting them `completed` (Codex 0.162 reports a SIGINT-ended user-shell turn as completed, `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V10.md` NEW ASSUMPTIONS 2) (Stage 2: LB-37), kills its shell commands and exits within 150 ms; a second SIGTERM exits immediately without killing shell commands.
  - `node fake-codex-tui.mjs --remote <ws url> [-c ...] [resume <id>]` — a TUI fake (Stage 2: LB-37, LB-39, LB-40, LB-41; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V8.md` §40, V9 NEW ASSUMPTIONS N5–N6, V10 NEW ASSUMPTIONS 2):
    - A `--remote` URL with a path other than `/` (for example `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/codex`) prints `Error: invalid remote address '<url>'; expected 'ws://host:port'` and exits 1, as Codex 0.162 does (Freshell's proxy URL has no path).
    - Prints `FAKE_TUI_READY thread=<id>`; on a writer conflict prints `This conversation is open in another app. Close it there and press R to continue here.` and stays running; when the startup `resume <id>` is answered `no rollout found`, prints `No saved session found with ID <id>` and exits 1.
    - Input `turn <text>` first starts an ephemeral title thread (`thread/start {ephemeral: true}`, one `turn/start` on it, then `thread/unsubscribe` once that turn completes, like the real TUI's per-turn title generation) and then starts a turn on its displayed thread; at that turn's completion it prints `FAKE_TUI_TURN_COMPLETED status=<status>` and writes BEL only when the status is `completed`.
    - Input `quit` exits 0 (also while a turn runs: Codex's "run in background" quit); `crash` exits 1 (a TUI crash); `resume <id>` switches the TUI to another thread (Codex's `/resume`), printing the same conflict line on an active-writer refusal; `fork` forks the current thread and switches to the child.
    - A connection that fails before the first successful open is a startup failure (exit 1). After that, a lost connection never ends the TUI: it prints `FAKE_TUI_RECONNECTING`, retries the same URL after 0, 1, 2 and 4 s and then every 8 s, and on success re-initializes, re-resumes its displayed thread and prints `FAKE_TUI_READY thread=<id>` again; when `FAKE_TUI_RECONNECT_DEADLINE_MS` (default 120000) passes without success it prints `Server connection could not be restored` and keeps running until `quit`.
  - `fake-codex-lock-holder <lock path>` (Rust, std only) (Stage 2: LB-11; R12; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V5.md` LB-11 acceptable path): creates the parent directory, opens the path read/write/create and calls `File::try_lock()` exactly as Codex's `rollout/src/writer_lock.rs` does (on Windows that is `LockFileEx` on a non-inheritable handle); prints `locked` and then waits until its stdin reaches end of file, or prints `conflict` and exits 1 when another process holds the lock. Off Linux the fake native starts one holder per held thread and keeps the holder's stdin pipe open for the thread's lifetime (unload or native exit ends it), so a lock that outlives Gone on Windows is detectable (Task 34).
