The earlier sketch's `before_signal_runs_first_and_on_gone_runs_before_the_handle_resolves` is replaced, because `before_signal` no longer exists (Stage 2: LB-31; R6). `conformance.rs` also gets these tests (each runs on every backend `backends()` / `backends_with_state()` returns unless it says otherwise; a test that asserts log events uses `#[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")]` so the thread-local capture layer sees the stop task's events):
- `stopping_is_persisted_before_any_signal_and_on_gone_runs_before_the_handle_resolves` (Stage 2: LB-31; R1, R6): a backend from `backends_with_state(tmp)`; right after `create_unit` the record file `<state root>/units/<id>.json` exists and parses as a `UnitRecord` in state `Running`; the agent runs with `exit_on_int` and `on_int_copy` = that record path; a Force `ShiftX` stop with `.operation("op-1")` and an `on_gone` that pushes `"gone:<reason>"` into a shared vector and notes whether the record file still exists. Asserts: `at-signal.json` parses as a `UnitRecord` whose state is `Stopping { reason: "shift-x", operation_id: Some("op-1"), .. }` (fails if Stopping were written after, or never before, the SIGINT); the vector is exactly `["gone:shift-x"]` and was filled before `wait()` returned; the record still existed while `on_gone` ran; the record file is gone once `wait()` returns.
- `the_codex_daemon_family_is_never_signalled` (Stage 2: LB-06, LB-46; R7; current-thread): agent with `daemon_family` and `managed_daemon_child`; Force `ShiftX`; after `wait_swept()`, the daemon, updater, installer and legacy stand-ins are alive with their original start times and none of them is in the survivor list, while main, setsid and nohup are dead; an INFO `unit.stop.spared` event was captured. The test then kills its own stand-ins through `ProcWatch::open_expecting(pid, start)`. Fails with the earlier argv-pair predicate (the updater, its installer child and the legacy launch die), which is what V3 observed on this host (`<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V3.md` Part 1).
- `a_pinned_root_is_stopped_even_when_the_backend_finds_no_members` (Stage 2: LB-16; R3): the test spawns `sleep 600` with a plain `tokio::process::Command` (no placement, no tag) and pins it with `add_root(ProcWatch::open(pid))`; a Force `ShiftX` stop; the sleep has exited by the time `wait()` returns. On the systemd backend (Task 5) the process is outside the slice, so only the direct root kill reaches it.
- `a_unit_refuses_members_once_its_stop_has_begun` (Stage 2: LB-16, LB-17; R3): with an agent running, start a Force stop; immediately `placement(MemberRole::Screen)` and `tokio_command(..)` return errors; a plain `sleep 600` spawned by the test and pinned with `set_screen` after the stop began exits (awaited through its `ProcWatch` with a 5 s deadline) without any further call; after `wait()`, `placement` still errors.
- `confirm_placement_accepts_members_and_rejects_strangers` (Stage 2: LB-27(c); R3): the placed agent main → `Ok(())`; a plain `sleep 600` child of the test (no tag, not pinned) → `Err`; after the test kills and reaps that sleep, `Err` with `ErrorKind::NotFound`.
- `an_untagged_child_reparented_during_the_grace_is_still_killed` (Stage 2: LB-44; tag backend only): agent with `untagged_child` and `exit_on_int`; Force `ShiftX`; the main exits on SIGINT, so the untagged child loses its parent link and carries no tag; after `wait_swept()` it is not alive. On macOS this fails without the pinned member snapshot taken before the soft signal; on Linux the reaper shim also keeps the child in the unit's tree.
- `a_detached_job_that_clears_its_environment_after_its_parent_exits_is_killed` (plan review R2-F1; `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, every backend `backends()` returns): agent with `envless_job`; the test waits (bounded, 10 s) until `/proc/<envless>/environ` is empty and the job's parent is no longer its intermediate; a Force `ShiftX`; after `wait_swept()` the job is not alive and is not in the survivor list. On the systemd backend the slice holds it; on the tag backend the job was reparented to the agent's reaper shim, whose tree is the unit. Fails with the tag-and-tree membership alone (no `--reaper` wrapper): the job has no tag and its parent is the init process.
- `a_user_kill_joining_a_weaker_stop_wins_its_reason` (Stage 2: LB-31; R6): (a) a Graceful `Cleanup` stop (grace 30 s) on an agent that ignores SIGTERM, joined after 100 ms by a Force `ShiftX`: the report says `reason == "shift-x"`, `mode == "force"`, `escalated`, and arrives within 2 s; (b) a Force `Respawn` joined by a Force `KillCommand` reports `"kill-command"`; (c) a Force `ShiftX` joined by a Force `Respawn` still reports `"shift-x"` (a weaker joiner never replaces the reason).
- `a_stop_that_panics_is_rerun_once_in_force_and_never_poisons_waiters` (Stage 2: LB-14; R2; current-thread, tag backend): a unit whose only process is a plain `sleep 600` pinned with `set_screen` (no main), stopped with Force `ShiftX`, a `soft_interrupt` that panics and an `on_gone` that increments a counter; two clones of the handle are awaited. Asserts: ERROR `unit.stop.panicked` was captured; both handles return the same report (no panic reaches a waiter); `on_gone` ran exactly once; the sleep has exited. Fails with the earlier sketch, whose `wait()` `expect`s a report and panics every waiter when the stop task dies.

#[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")]
async fn an_unconfirmed_stop_logs_an_error_at_five_seconds_and_keeps_waiting() {

    std::env::set_var("FRESHELL_TEST_UNIT_GONE_DELAY_MS", "6500");

    let c = Containment::tag_backend(SelectOptions::default());
    let unit = c.create_unit(UnitId::mint(), UnitLabel { provider: "test".into(), ..Default::default() }).unwrap();
    let s = agent_script(&AgentOpts { exit_on_int: true, ..Default::default() });
    let _child = spawn_main(&unit, &s).await;
    read_pids(&s).await;
    let handle = unit.stop(StopRequest::new(StopMode::Force, StopReason::ShiftX, "test"));

    assert!(cap.has(tracing::Level::ERROR, "unit.stop.unconfirmed"));

`crates/freshell-containment/src/backend/mod.rs`:

```rust
use std::io;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::process::ProcIdentity;
use crate::unit::{MemberRole, Placement};
use crate::{BoxFuture, UnitId};

#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) mod tag;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub(crate) mod roots;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum BackendKind {
    SystemdScope,
    LinuxTag,
    WindowsJob,
    MacosTag,
}

impl BackendKind {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::SystemdScope => "systemd-scope",
            Self::LinuxTag => "linux-tag",
            Self::WindowsJob => "windows-job",
            Self::MacosTag => "macos-tag",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct Capability {
    pub kind: BackendKind,
    /// true = membership is kernel-tracked (cgroup / job); false = tag + tree.
    pub full: bool,
    pub reason: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct KillSummary {
    pub killed: usize,
    pub spared: Vec<ProcIdentity>,
}
```

The rest of `backend/mod.rs` is the two crate-private traits exactly as listed under Interfaces (Stage 2: LB-01, LB-16, LB-27, LB-46, LB-49; R1, R3, R7, R8). Compared with the earlier sketch: `Backend::reopen` returns the unit for a recorded id unconditionally (no existence probe) and `Backend::surviving` is deleted, because nothing may enumerate units beyond this server's own records; `UnitBackend::kill_all` becomes asynchronous (`self: Arc<Self>`, owned `roots`, a `BoxFuture`) so the systemd backend can wait for `frozen 1` through inotify with a deadline; `UnitBackend::confirm_placement(pid, roots)` is new; `UnitBackend::remove(emptied)` returns `io::Result<()>` and receives whether the post-Gone emptiness event arrived (the systemd backend stops the slice only then). `log_spared` is deleted: backends return spared identities in `KillSummary.spared` and the unit logs them through `events::spared` with its keys, by process name and pid, never argv (V12 showed `scrub()` lets argv secrets through and can break JSON lines: `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V12.md` §LB-46a).

`crates/freshell-containment/src/backend/tag.rs` (`cfg(unix)`). The earlier code sketch is withdrawn: it enumerated every tagged process at boot (`surviving`), reopened a unit only when something still carried its tag, spared only argv containing both `app-server` and `--managed-daemon`, and sent SIGSTOP/SIGKILL/SIGCONT to bare pids (Stage 2: LB-01, LB-02, LB-06, LB-44, LB-46; R1, R7; finder §6 Task 4). The tag backend (Linux without a user systemd manager; macOS) implements the two traits as follows:
- `TagBackend { kind, reason }`: `capability()` is `{ kind, full: false, reason: Some(reason) }`. `create(id)` and `reopen(id)` both return `TagUnit::new(UNIT_ENV, id.as_str())`; `reopen` does not look for processes first, because its caller holds a recorded id. Tags carry no per-server namespace: nothing enumerates tags any more, and every lookup is by a recorded, unique unit id. On Linux, when the backend was built with a shim (`SelectOptions.shim`: the server always passes one, Task 12, and the conformance support passes the test build), `placement(role, _)` returns the wrapper `[<shim exe>, <shim leading args...>, "--reaper", "--"]` plus the tag env, so every member the unit spawns is a reaper shim whose tree holds everything it starts (plan review R2-F1); without a shim (tests in other crates that do not exercise membership) it returns the tag env only, and `capability().reason` ends with `; no reaper shim`. macOS placement is Task 7's.
- `TagUnit { key, value }` membership is computed fresh at each call from one-shot `/proc` (macOS: libproc, Task 7) reads, never by polling. Candidates are every process other than the server itself whose environment carries `key=value`, plus the live pinned roots passed in, plus every descendant (`process::children`) of those. A process whose environment cannot be read is not a tag member, though it can still be a member as a root's descendant. The count of such same-uid processes is logged once per call at INFO (`event=unit.members.environ_withheld`, `unit_id`, `count`) instead of silently treating them as untagged (finder §6 Task 4, the promise at Task 2's `environ_value`).
- Sparing (R7): a candidate whose OWN argv satisfies `is_codex_daemon_family`, and every descendant of a spared process, is spared. Spared processes are excluded from `members()`, never stopped or signalled, and returned (as `ProcIdentity`, with name, pid and start) in `KillSummary.spared`. Because each family member is judged by its own argv, sibling roots (the daemon and its updater, V3 NA-1) and a lone updater are covered. A daemon a pane started carries the pane's whole environment, tag included (V3 NA-4), so it is always a spared member and never re-stopped.
- `kill_all(roots)` is a stop-the-world sweep, run on a blocking task, that never signals a bare pid. In rounds (at most 64, ending when a round finds no new candidate), it opens a `ProcWatch` for each new non-spared candidate, skipping processes already gone. It then re-verifies that the pinned incarnation is a member (its tag, or its parent is a member or root), checking afterwards that the watch has not exited, so the read referred to that incarnation. Finally it sends SIGSTOP through the watch. A stopped process cannot fork, exit or exec, so the set converges. Then each stopped process's argv is read again: a daemon-family process (one that exec'd between check and stop) is resumed with SIGCONT through its watch and spared, and every other stopped process gets SIGKILL through its watch. The result is `KillSummary { killed, spared }`.
- With reaper roots, the "every descendant of a pinned root" part of the candidate rule is kept by the kernel: an orphaned descendant is reparented to the nearest living subreaper ancestor, which is its pane's shim, so the tag and the snapshot of step (b) only matter for a shim that something outside Freshell killed. The rule itself is unchanged.
- `members(roots)` returns the non-spared candidates' identities. `confirm_placement(pid, roots)` returns `Ok(())` when the process carries `key=value`, or is a pinned root or a descendant of one; `ErrorKind::NotFound` when it is gone; otherwise an error saying it is not in the unit. `wait_empty()` returns `None` (no kernel-tracked emptiness). `remove(_)` returns `Ok(())`.

`crates/freshell-containment/src/reaper.rs` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`; plan review R2-F1) holds `pub(crate) fn run(program: &OsStr, args: &[OsString]) -> i32`, which `exec_shim::unit_exec_main` calls on Linux when `--reaper` appears before `--` (other OSes ignore the flag; no backend there places with it). Checked first on this host with a stand-in (`<logs_dir>/scratch/subreaper/`, Decision 19). In order:

1. `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, 1)`. On failure it writes the OS error to stderr and returns 126 before starting anything, so the member exits before its placement is confirmed: a typed start failure (R3).
2. Block SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT, then start the command as its child with `std::process::Command` (std resets the child's signal mask, so the command starts with nothing blocked) and a `pre_exec` (async-signal-safe calls only) that calls `setpgid(0, 0)` and, when fd 0 is the shim's controlling terminal and the shim's group is its foreground group, ignores SIGTTOU, makes the new group the terminal's foreground group (`tcsetpgrp`) and restores SIGTTOU's default before exec. The shim makes the same `setpgid` and `tcsetpgrp` calls on its side, the usual shell order, so neither side races. A screen's shim is the PTY session leader portable-pty made it (`setsid` + `TIOCSCTTY`), so the agent stays in that session and owns the terminal's foreground group: a Ctrl+C or a resize the user makes reaches the agent, never the shim.
3. Install handlers for SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT that forward the signal to the child's pid (`kill(2)`, async-signal-safe), then unblock them, so a signal that arrived while the command was starting is forwarded too. So the stop sequence's soft signal to a pane whose main is its screen (the shim) reaches the agent once, and a PTY hangup's SIGHUP to the session leader reaches the agent as it does today.
4. Reap every child with `waitpid(-1)` (adopted orphans included) until the command itself exits.
5. Kill what is left of its own tree with the tag backend's stop-the-world sweep (shared code; descendants found from `/proc` parent links by one-shot reads), sparing the Codex daemon family by each process's own argv plus its descendants. It does not wait for the killed processes; whoever adopts them reaps them, so neither the shim's exit nor Gone waits on a descendant stuck in the kernel.
6. Exit with the command's exit code; when a signal ended the command, reset that signal to its default and raise it on itself, so the PTY reader and the stop sequence see the same status the command produced (Decision 13's screen-exit rules read it).

The shim never reads or writes the terminal and holds no state beyond the child's pid.

`crates/freshell-containment/tests/reaper.rs` (`#![cfg(target_os = "linux")]`; plan review R2-F1). Each test starts the test shim (`support::test_shim()`) with `--reaper -- bash <script>` through `portable-pty` (`native_pty_system().openpty(..)`, `slave.spawn_command(..)`), the same `setsid` + `TIOCSCTTY` child setup Freshell's screens get; the script records its own pid, `ps -o pgid=,tpgid=,sid=`, and the pids of what it starts, and traps INT (one marker line per INT, exit 0 on the second). Every process signalled is one the test started, through a start-time-pinned `ProcWatch`:
- `ctrl_c_typed_into_the_pane_reaches_only_the_agent`: writing `\x03` to the PTY master adds exactly one INT marker line; the shim is still running; the agent's pgid equals the terminal's foreground group and its session id is the shim's pid.
- `the_shim_keeps_a_detached_job_that_cleared_its_environment_and_kills_it_when_the_agent_ends`: the script also starts the `envless_job` shape and a `nohup sleep 600`; once the job's environment is empty its parent is the shim; then SIGINT to the shim (the stop's soft signal to a screen main): the agent's second INT ends it with code 0, the shim's exit status is 0, and within a bounded 5 s wait the detached job and the `nohup` job are gone.
- `a_pty_hangup_ends_the_agent_and_the_shim_reports_its_signal`: dropping the PTY master ends the agent (SIGHUP forwarded); the shim's wait status is "killed by SIGHUP"; the detached job is gone.
- `the_shim_spares_the_codex_daemon_family`: the script starts a `perl -e 'sleep 600' app-server --managed-daemon` stand-in and then exits on its own; the stand-in is still alive with its original start time after the shim exits, and the test then kills it through its watch.

`crates/freshell-containment/src/backend/roots.rs` (Windows placeholder until Task 6, which deletes it). It implements both traits with no member tracking. `create(id)`/`reopen(id)` return a unit whose `placement` only adds the tag; `kill_all` returns an empty summary; `members` is empty; `wait_empty` is `None`; `remove` is `Ok(())`; `confirm_placement` returns `ErrorKind::Unsupported`. Nothing executes on Windows before Task 6; only the cross-target check compiles it. The earlier sketch's `surviving` and `Option`-returning `reopen` are gone (Stage 2: LB-01; R1, R3).

`crates/freshell-containment/src/record.rs` (new; Stage 2: LB-01, LB-02; R1) holds `UnitRecord` and `UnitRecordState`, exactly as listed under Interfaces, plus the crate-private store:
- `open(state_root)` creates `<state_root>/units/`. An empty `state_root` gives the in-memory store (tests only). A create failure gives a store that is not open: ERROR `containment.unit_store_unavailable` (path, cause) once, and every `write` returns that error. There is no store-wide lock (plan review R1-F1).
- `write(&UnitRecord)`: on a unit's first write, create and `try_lock` `<unit id>.lock` and keep it open in the store (unit ids are minted fresh, so the lock is free); then write a temp file in the same directory and rename it to `<unit id>.json`. `remove(&UnitId)` deletes `<unit id>.json`, then releases, closes and deletes `<unit id>.lock`.
- `load_all()` (boot only): for every `*.json`, open (creating if absent) and `try_lock` its `<unit id>.lock`. A lock held elsewhere means a running server owns that record: it is skipped, never read. A lock taken means no running server owns it: the record is read, the lock is kept (this server now owns it) and the record is returned. A file that does not parse can only be a torn write after a machine crash, whose processes are gone with it, so it is logged at WARN `containment.unit_record_unreadable` and removed with its lock file. Lock files without a record are ignored.
- The in-memory store keeps the same records in a map; `load_all()` returns nothing.

`crates/freshell-containment/src/unit.rs`. One coding-agent pane is one unit, and `AgentUnit::stop` is the ONLY stop sequence. Running/Stopping/Gone stay in the owner registry; the unit runs and joins the in-flight stop and keeps the unit's persisted record, where persisted Stopping lives (R1). The earlier sketch's imports, `UnitLabel`, `StopRequest`, `StopHandle` and `AgentUnit` are replaced by the prose after this block (Stage 2: LB-14, LB-16, LB-17, LB-28, LB-31, LB-44; R1, R2, R3, R6). These items stay exactly as sketched:

```rust
pub const FORCE_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
pub const UNCONFIRMED_AFTER: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);
pub const POST_GONE_EMPTY_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemberRole {
    Screen,
    Agent,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Placement {
    pub wrapper: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub env: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StopMode {
    Force,
    Graceful { grace: Duration },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StopReason {
    ShiftX,
    KillCommand,
    Respawn,
    Cleanup,
    Handoff,
    StuckRestart,
    StartCancelled,
    AgentExited { exit_code: Option<i64> },
    BootFinish,
    ServerShutdown,
}

impl StopReason {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::ShiftX => "shift-x",
            Self::KillCommand => "kill-command",
            Self::Respawn => "respawn",
            Self::Cleanup => "cleanup",
            Self::Handoff => "handoff",
            Self::StuckRestart => "stuck-restart",
            Self::StartCancelled => "start-cancelled",
            Self::AgentExited { .. } => "agent-exited",
            Self::BootFinish => "boot-finish",
            Self::ServerShutdown => "server-shutdown",
        }
    }
}

pub type GoneCallback = Box<dyn FnOnce(StopReport) -> BoxFuture<'static, ()> + Send>;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StopReport {
    pub unit_id: UnitId,
    pub reason: String,
    pub mode: &'static str,
    pub duration_ms: u64,
    pub escalated: bool,
    pub lock_released: bool,
}
```

The rest of `unit.rs` is specified here in prose; the earlier code is withdrawn (Stage 2: LB-14, LB-16, LB-17, LB-28, LB-31, LB-44; R1, R2, R3, R6, R9).

Constants and types:
- `pub const PLACEMENT_DEADLINE: Duration = 2 s` sits beside the three constants above (no persist deadline: step (a) awaits the write; plan review R1-F1).
- `UnitLabel { provider: String, session_id: Option<String>, terminal_id: Option<String>, mode: String, create_request_id: Option<String> }` derives `Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq`.
- `StopRequest` keeps `mode`, `reason`, `initiator`, `operation_id`, `on_gone` and `soft_interrupt`, with the builders `new`, `operation`, `on_gone` and `soft_interrupt` as sketched before; the `before_signal` field and builder are gone.
- `StopHandle` keeps `gone` and `swept` watch receivers and the methods `wait`, `wait_for`, `try_report` and `wait_swept`. `wait()` never `expect`s a report. When the stop task can no longer produce one, `wait()` stays pending (the unconfirmed case); the sender is kept alive in the unit, so a closed channel can never be mistaken for Gone.

`AgentUnit` (a `Clone` over an `Arc`):
- **State.** The unit keeps:
  - its id, backend, capability and label;
  - the screen and main watches, the extra root watches and the lock paths;
  - the member-spawn sequence;
  - the unit record (the current `UnitRecord` behind a mutex, plus the store handle);
  - the single stop slot, holding the handle, the escalation flag and notify, the stop's current (strongest) reason and mode, and the stop's `on_gone` and `soft_interrupt`.

  Record writes are serialized under the record mutex. Once the record is deleted, no later write recreates it.
- **Accessors.** `id`, `label`, `capability`, `screen`, `main`, `main_is_screen`, `set_lock_paths`, `members` and `stop_in_flight` behave as sketched before.
- **Record upkeep (R1).**
  - `set_label` also rewrites the record's terminal id and create-request id. When the label has a session id, it appends `(provider, session_id)` to the record's conversation keys.
  - `note_conversation(provider, session_id)` appends one key; nothing is written when the key is already there.
  - `set_screen` and `set_main` replace the previous screen or main identity in the record's roots with the new `(pid, start)`; `add_root` appends one. So the record holds only current roots.
  - A record write failure is logged at ERROR (`events::record_write_failed`, op `update`) and does not fail the call.
- **Members refused once the stop has begun (R3; LB-16, LB-17).**
  - `placement()` and `tokio_command()` return an `io::Error` ("unit <id> is stopping").
  - A watch pinned by `set_screen`, `set_main` or `add_root` after the stop began gets SIGKILL through that watch inside the call once Stopping is saved; while the step (a) write is still outstanding it is only pinned as a root, and step (d) kills it (plan review R1-F1: no signal before Stopping is saved). So a start racing a Shift-X never leaves a process behind, whatever order its caller spawns and pins in.
  - Units are never reused after a stop: each start attempt gets a fresh unit (Task 10).
- **`confirm_placement(pid)`.** Calls the backend's `confirm_placement(pid, root pids)`. Callers (Tasks 10–12, 23) run it once at the start's settle point: the sidecar right after its readiness probe; screens and other agents when they settle, or at the latest at `PLACEMENT_DEADLINE`. An error is a typed start failure logged through `events::placement_failed`, never an agent exit or a screen restart (R3; V2 showed a failed `systemd-run` exits 1 exactly like a crashed agent, `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V2.md` §LB-27(c)).
- **`stop(req)` is single-flight.**
  - The first call logs `unit.stop.requested` and moves the request's `on_gone` and `soft_interrupt` into the stop slot. It then spawns the supervised stop and returns its handle.
  - A later call joins the stop in flight. A Force join sets the escalation flag: a Graceful stop skips its remaining grace, and a Force stop still inside its 1 s grace skips the rest. The report's mode becomes `"force"`.
  - A `ShiftX` or `KillCommand` join on a `Respawn`, `StuckRestart`, `Handoff` or `Cleanup` stop replaces the stop's reason. The persisted Stopping reason is rewritten too; a failed rewrite is logged at ERROR `unit.stop.persist_failed` and the Stopping state already saved stands.
  - The joining request's own `on_gone`, `soft_interrupt` and `operation_id` are dropped; a joiner that needs Gone awaits the returned handle (R6).
- **Supervision (R2; LB-14).** The sequence below runs as attempt 1 in its own task, which a supervisor task awaits.
  - Attempt 1 can end in a panic or an error. A panic is logged at ERROR `unit.stop.panicked`. An error, such as EMFILE from a watch registration (the stop path has no `expect` or `unwrap` on fallible OS calls), is logged at ERROR `unit.stop.failed`.
  - Either way, the supervisor re-runs the sequence once as attempt 2 in Force mode, and attempt 2 uses whichever stop-slot callbacks attempt 1 had not yet taken. `on_gone` is taken only at Gone, so a panic before Gone still runs it once. A panic inside `on_gone` is final.
  - When attempt 2 also panics or fails, the log line carries `final_attempt: true`. No report is ever published. The record stays Stopping, the unit keeps refusing members, and the next boot finishes the unit (Task 19).
  - A stop task dropped by runtime shutdown leaves the record Stopping the same way.
- **One attempt, in order:**
  a. **Persist (R6; plan review R1-F1).** Write `Stopping { reason, operation_id, since_ms }` to the record on a blocking task and await the write's completion; there is no deadline, and nothing is signalled until the write has succeeded, so a crash at any point leaves either a Running record whose processes were never signalled (the next boot treats the unit as running: the kill was never carried out) or a Stopping record (the next boot finishes it). The test hook `testing::persist_delay()` delays the write before the record lock is taken. A write error is logged at ERROR `unit.stop.persist_failed` and the attempt waits without signalling: the stop stays in flight (the registry keeps the conversation Stopping, the unit keeps refusing members), the client shows "Stopping…" after 5 s as for any unconfirmed stop, and the next Force request on the unit (a second Shift-X or kill command, a cleanup escalation, the shutdown join) retries the write once; the sequence goes on only after a successful write. A record already Stopping (a boot finish of a stop interrupted by a restart) is left as it is. The in-memory store (tests) never fails.
  b. **Snapshot (non-full backends only; LB-44).** Pin every current member with `ProcWatch::open_expecting(pid, start)`, skipping members that cannot be pinned. Members that lose both their tag and their parent link during the grace are still killed in step d. One example is an MCP server Codex starts with an environment allow-list, which is reparented when the native exits.
  c. **Soft phase.** As in the earlier sketch:
     - Force: SIGINT the main (else run `soft_interrupt`, else log signal `none`), then wait for the main's exit, `FORCE_GRACE`, or a Force join.
     - Graceful: SIGTERM the main, then wait for its exit, its grace, or a Force join. Reaching the grace, or a Force join, logs WARN `unit.stop.escalated`.
  d. **Kill (R3).** Run the backend's `kill_all(root pids)`, which kills the whole unit and spares the daemon family; spared processes are logged at INFO through `events::spared`. A failure is logged at ERROR `unit.stop.kill_all_failed`, as before. Then SIGKILL, through its watch, the screen, the main, every pinned root and every snapshot member that the daemon-family rule does not spare. So a unit whose slice or job does not exist yet is still stopped, and a wrapper killed before it placed itself can place nothing afterwards. This kill is the last signal of the sequence, and the unconfirmed clock starts here.
  e. **Confirm (R6, R9; LB-28; V4 N1).**
     - Wait, event-driven, for the main, the screen and every non-spared pinned root to exit; then apply the test hook `gone_delay`.
     - Run the lock check, which comes after the whole-unit kill and never at the main's first exit event. When lock paths are set, ask Task 3's member-scoped fd lookup (`lock_holders_among(paths, member pids)`) which unit members still hold any of them; spared processes are not members. SIGKILL each such holder through a pinned watch, wait for its exit, then check once more.
     - `lock_released` is true when no member holds a lock path. A holder outside the unit is not part of Gone; Task 16 reports it when a reopen meets it.
     - If confirmation is not complete `UNCONFIRMED_AFTER` after step d's kill, log ERROR `unit.stop.unconfirmed` once and keep waiting. While step (a) has not yet saved Stopping, the same ERROR is logged once `UNCONFIRMED_AFTER` after the request.
  f. **Gone.** Build the report: the stop's current reason, its mode, the duration since the request, `escalated` and `lock_released`. Log `unit.stop.gone`. Take and run `on_gone`. Delete the record; a failure is logged as `record_write_failed` with op `remove`. Then publish the report to every handle.
- **Sweep, after Gone.** Run `kill_all` again plus the root kills, for anything that appeared since. Wait for the backend's emptiness event, bounded by `POST_GONE_EMPTY_WAIT`. Log members still running at WARN `unit.descendants.survived` (Task 2: names, pids and start times, never argv). Then call `remove(emptied)`, where `emptied` says whether the emptiness event arrived; a failure is logged at WARN `unit.release_failed`. The survivor list is published to `wait_swept()`.

`crates/freshell-containment/src/containment.rs`. `ShimCommand` and the process-global handle stay exactly as sketched:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ShimCommand {
    pub exe: PathBuf,
    pub leading_args: Vec<String>,
}

static GLOBAL: OnceLock<Containment> = OnceLock::new();

/// Install the process-global containment (freshell-server main, once).
pub fn set_global_containment(c: Containment) -> bool {
    GLOBAL.set(c).is_ok()
}

pub fn global_containment() -> Option<Containment> {
    GLOBAL.get().cloned()
}
```

The rest of `containment.rs` is specified in prose; the earlier code is withdrawn because it reopened units by enumerating survivors and pinned roots without their start times (Stage 2: LB-01, LB-02; R1):
- `SelectOptions { shim: Option<ShimCommand>, state_root: PathBuf }` derives `Debug, Clone, Default`. The `shim` doc comment stays as sketched: the server passes its own exe plus `__unit-exec`; tests pass the `freshell-unit-exec` bin. `state_root` is described under Interfaces.
- `Containment` holds the backend (`Arc<dyn Backend>`) and the record store (`Arc`).
- `select(opts)` first opens the store from `opts.state_root`. It then probes exactly as the earlier sketch did: the Linux arm returns the tag backend with reason "no systemd user manager backend" until Task 5 inserts the systemd probe; macOS returns the macOS tag backend; Windows returns the roots placeholder. It logs `event=containment.backend` once (backend, full, reason). A degraded selection never blocks a kill.
- `tag_backend(opts)` is the forced tag backend (reason "forced tag backend") with the store from `opts.state_root`. `capability()` is unchanged.
- `create_unit(id, label)` creates the backend unit. It then writes the Running record built from the label BEFORE returning: provider, mode, terminal id, create-request id, the label's session id as the first conversation key, and no roots. A write failure, or a store that is not open, returns the error; nothing has spawned yet.
- `recorded_units()` returns the records `load_all()` took ownership of at open: those no running server holds. It is the only way units are found after a restart: nothing enumerates slices, tags, jobs or processes beyond a recorded unit id, and `surviving_units()` is deleted.
- `reopen_unit(&record, label)` calls the backend's `reopen(record.unit_id)`. It returns an `AgentUnit` that continues that record without rewriting it, using `label` for its log keys. Every recorded root is pinned with `ProcWatch::open_expecting(pid, start)` and added as a root. A root that cannot be pinned (gone, or alive with a different start time) is not pinned and is never signalled; it is logged at WARN `unit.root.not_pinned`. (LB-02)
- `adopt_legacy(tag_key, tag_value, roots: &[(u32, u64)], label)` is for v1 Codex records. On Unix its backend is a `TagUnit` on the legacy tag; Task 6 gives Windows its own form. It gets a freshly minted unit id with a Running record, and its roots are pinned exactly as in `reopen_unit`. The residual: a v1 sidecar was started without a reaper shim, so a legacy unit's members are found through the legacy tag, the pinned roots and their descendants only, and a crash during a legacy stop leaves a record whose next-boot finish finds members only through the pinned roots and their descendants.

  - Slice: `freshell-n<ns>-<unit id>.slice`, where `<unit id>` is `UnitId::as_str()` (`u` + 32 hex). systemd nests it under `freshell-n<ns>.slice` → `freshell.slice` in the user manager.

The env adds `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` (captured at probe) and `FRESHELL_UNIT_ID`. (Stage 2: LB-27; V1 NA-3)
- No `busctl` is used anywhere. Daemon-family members are never moved out of the slice; they are spared in place. (Stage 2: LB-49; R7)

//! systemd backend specifics. On hosts with a user manager (garageserver)
//! FRESHELL_REQUIRE_SYSTEMD_CONTAINMENT=1 makes the
//! selection itself a hard requirement; elsewhere these tests assert the
//! degraded selection instead, so they never silently pass on nothing.
mod support;

use std::time::Duration;

use freshell_containment::*;
use support::*;

fn require() -> bool {
    std::env::var("FRESHELL_REQUIRE_SYSTEMD_CONTAINMENT").as_deref() == Ok("1")
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn selection_matches_the_host() {
    let c = Containment::select(SelectOptions::default());
    if require() {
        assert_eq!(c.capability().kind, BackendKind::SystemdScope);
        assert!(c.capability().full);
    } else if c.capability().kind != BackendKind::SystemdScope {
        assert_eq!(c.capability().kind, BackendKind::LinuxTag);
        assert!(c.capability().reason.is_some(), "a degraded selection names why");
    }
}

fn systemd_or_skip_reason() -> Option<Containment> {
    let c = Containment::select(SelectOptions::default());
    (c.capability().kind == BackendKind::SystemdScope).then_some(c)
}
```

`crates/freshell-containment/src/backend/inotify.rs`:

```rust
//! Event-driven waits on cgroup v2 `cgroup.events` (populated / frozen).
//! The kernel raises a file-modified event when either value changes.
use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd, OwnedFd};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

fn read_flag(events: &Path, key: &str) -> Option<u8> {
    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(events).ok()?;
    raw.lines().find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(key)?.trim().parse().ok())
}

/// Resolve when `<dir>/cgroup.events` shows `key value` (or the cgroup is gone).
pub(crate) async fn wait_flag(dir: PathBuf, key: &'static str, value: u8) {
    let events = dir.join("cgroup.events");
    let fd = unsafe { libc::inotify_init1(libc::IN_NONBLOCK | libc::IN_CLOEXEC) };
    if fd < 0 {
        return;
    }
    let fd = unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd) };
    let c = std::ffi::CString::new(events.as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes()).unwrap();
    let wd = unsafe { libc::inotify_add_watch(fd.as_raw_fd(), c.as_ptr(), libc::IN_MODIFY | libc::IN_DELETE_SELF) };
    // Watch first, then check: no lost wake-up.
    if wd < 0 || read_flag(&events, key).is_none_or(|v| v == value) {
        return;
    }
    let Ok(afd) = tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::with_interest(fd, tokio::io::Interest::READABLE) else { return };
    loop {
        let Ok(mut guard) = afd.readable().await else { return };
        let mut buf = [0u8; 4096];
        loop {
            let n = unsafe { libc::read(afd.get_ref().as_raw_fd(), buf.as_mut_ptr().cast(), buf.len()) };
            if n <= 0 {
                break;
            }
        }
        guard.clear_ready();
        if read_flag(&events, key).is_none_or(|v| v == value) {
            return;
        }
    }
}
```

`wait_flag` stays exactly as sketched above. Every caller bounds it with a deadline (`tokio::time::timeout`): the post-Gone sweep with `POST_GONE_EMPTY_WAIT`, and the freeze wait below with 1 s. A waiter armed on a cgroup that is removed gets no event at all, so an unbounded caller could hang forever (Stage 2: LB-05 caveats; R8; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V2.md` NA-05-2).

`crates/freshell-containment/src/backend/systemd.rs` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`) covers Linux with a reachable user systemd manager: one transient SLICE per unit and one SCOPE per member spawn. `systemd-run --user --scope` places itself, then execs the command with the same pid; this is race-free and works for portable-pty children that offer no pre_exec hook. V1 confirmed it keeps the pid, the PTY session and a clean signal state at about 40 ms per spawn, from both the service and the SSH-session context (`<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V1.md` §LB-03). The slices are siblings of the server's own unit, so units survive a server restart, including a stop or restart of a `KillMode=control-group` unit (V1 §LB-04). These helpers stay as sketched:

```rust
const CGROUP_ROOT: &str = "/sys/fs/cgroup";

fn which(name: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    std::env::var_os("PATH")?
        .to_str()?
        .split(':')
        .map(|d| Path::new(d).join(name))
        .find(|p| p.is_file())
}

fn procs_recursive(dir: &Path, out: &mut Vec<u32>) {
    if let Ok(raw) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("cgroup.procs")) {
        out.extend(raw.split_whitespace().filter_map(|p| p.parse::<u32>().ok()));
    }
    if let Ok(rd) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
        for e in rd.flatten() {
            if e.file_type().is_ok_and(|t| t.is_dir()) {
                procs_recursive(&e.path(), out);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The rest of `systemd.rs` is specified in prose. The earlier sketch is withdrawn: its shared `freshell-agents` naming, `surviving`, existence-gated `reopen`, deadline-less probe, `busctl` eviction, freeze without a wait, per-unit sequence-only scope names and no-op `remove` were each falsified or simplified in Stage 2 (LB-01, LB-27, LB-49; R1, R3, R7, R8).
- **Probe.** `SystemdBackend::probe(opts: &SelectOptions) -> Result<SystemdBackend, String>` runs once, at `select`.
  - In order, it checks:
    - cgroup v2 is mounted (`cgroup.controllers` exists);
    - `systemd-run` and `systemctl` are on `PATH` (`busctl` is no longer needed);
    - `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is set.
  - It captures the bus env. `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` defaults to `unix:path=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`.
  - It runs `systemd-run --version`. The number on its first line decides whether the wrapper adds `--expand-environment=no` (254 or newer).
  - It runs `systemctl --user show -p ControlGroup --value`, which must print a non-empty manager cgroup.
  - It derives `<ns>` from the canonical `state_root` and mints the per-boot nonce.
  - It places a throwaway scope: `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect [--expand-environment=no] --slice=freshell-n<ns>-probe.slice -- cat /proc/self/cgroup`. The output must contain `/freshell.slice/freshell-n<ns>.slice/freshell-n<ns>-probe.slice/`.
  - It runs `systemctl --user stop freshell-n<ns>-probe.slice`, because implicit slices are never collected (V2 §LB-27(a)); a failure here is only a WARN.
  - Every command runs with a 10 s deadline and captures stdout and stderr. On timeout, the probe kills and reaps its own child.
  - Any failing step fails the attempt. The whole probe is retried once. A second failure selects the tag backend, with a reason naming the step and its error, or `timed out`. V2 measured a stalled bus blocking each command for 90 s (§LB-27(d)).
  - The earlier `run_ok` helper becomes this deadline-bounded runner.
- **Naming, `create` and `reopen` (R1).** `create(id)` and `reopen(id)` both return the `SystemdUnit` for the slice path under Interfaces. `reopen` does not check that the directory exists, so a unit already gone simply stops at once. `surviving` is gone.
- **`placement(role, seq)`.** The wrapper and env listed under Interfaces: the scope name carries the role, the boot nonce and the per-unit sequence.
- **`confirm_placement(pid, _roots)`.** Reads `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` once and returns:
  - `Ok(())` when its `0::` path lies under the unit's slice path;
  - `ErrorKind::NotFound` when the file cannot be read (the process is gone);
  - otherwise an error naming the cgroup path where the process actually is.

  This one read turns a `systemd-run` that failed or stalled into a typed start failure, instead of the exit code 1 a crashed agent also produces (V2 NA-27-4).
- **Sparing (R7).** Within the slice's pids (`procs_recursive`), a pid is spared when its own argv satisfies `is_codex_daemon_family`. Every pid whose parent is spared is spared too, iterating to a fixed point over the snapshot.
- **`kill_all(roots)` (R7, R8; LB-49).**
  - If the slice directory does not exist yet, return an empty summary; the unit kills its pinned roots itself.
  - Otherwise write `1` to the slice's `cgroup.freeze`. Wait for `frozen 1` with `inotify::wait_flag(<slice dir>, "frozen ", 1)` under a 1 s deadline; on timeout, continue and log WARN `unit.stop.freeze_timeout` with `unit_id`.
  - Snapshot the slice's pids and compute the spared set.
  - If the snapshot holds spared processes: send SIGKILL to every non-spared pid through `ProcWatch::open(pid)`, then write `0` to `cgroup.freeze`. Frozen tasks cannot fork, exit or exec, and a fatal signal kills a frozen task. V2 observed every non-spared member die within about 1 ms while the slice stayed frozen, and the spared stand-in run on after the thaw (§"Supporting observation: LB-49 premise"). The spared processes resume in place, and the slice stays populated by them.
  - Otherwise: write `1` to `cgroup.kill`, then write `0` to `cgroup.freeze`. If the `cgroup.kill` write fails, fall back to `systemctl --user kill --signal=SIGKILL <slice>` under the 10 s deadline, which V2 confirmed works on a slice (§LB-05(a)).
  - Return `{ killed, spared identities }`.
  - Nothing is moved out of the slice, so Codex's managed daemon is never modified (constraint 45).
  - Residual, recorded: a slice holding a pane-started daemon stays populated by the daemon, and by all later daemon work for any client (V3 NA-2); the slice is not stopped.
- **`members(_roots)`.** The slice's pids minus the spared ones, as identities.
- **`wait_empty()`.** `inotify::wait_flag(<slice dir>, "populated ", 0)`.
- **`remove(emptied)` (R8).** When `emptied` and the slice directory still exists, run `systemctl --user stop <slice>` under the 10 s deadline on a blocking thread, and return its error for the unit to log. When not emptied (spared daemon or survivors), leave the slice running and return `Ok(())`; the unit has already logged the spared processes and the survivors. Implicit slices are never collected otherwise, so without this every stopped pane would leave an active, empty slice for the life of the user manager (V2 §LB-27(a)).
- **Event waits (LB-05 caveats; V2 NA-05-1..3).** Every wait watches the unit SLICE's `cgroup.events` only, never a scope directory: a scope can be removed before its deferred notification fires. Every wait has a deadline. Gone never depends on seeing a transient `populated 0`, because events coalesce within about 10 ms.

### Task 6: Windows Job Object backend, self-placing exec shim, Windows process facts

Design decisions (Stage 2: LB-08, LB-09, LB-10, LB-11, LB-15, LB-26; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V5.md` §3–§6):
- Steps 1–4 run V5's early tests on `windows-2022` BEFORE any backend code exists, and their outcome picks the unit job's flags (decision rule in Step 4):
  - **Branch A** (a non-detached Node grandchild stays in a unit job that has `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK`, and a Node-launched explicit-breakaway daemon leaves it): unit job = `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE | BREAKAWAY_OK`; a stop is `TerminateJobObject`; Codex's managed daemon and its updater (Codex 0.162 starts both with `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`, V5 §5) are never unit members, so neither kill-on-close at server exit nor a stop reaches them (LB-10 holds).
  - **Branch B** (otherwise): unit job = `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` only, so silent breakaways stop at the unit job and every Node grandchild stays contained. A pane-started Codex daemon then stays inside the unit job (Codex's accepted "residual job"), so the backend watches `JOB_OBJECT_MSG_NEW_PROCESS`; when a daemon-family process (R7: `is_codex_daemon_family` on that process's own command line) joins, it clears `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` for that unit, and that unit's stop is per member: terminate every non-spared member, re-enumerating on each new-process message until only spared members remain, and log the spared pids by name. From the moment kill-on-close is cleared, the unit record is the boot path to the unit's members (next bullet).
  - Blocking findings (Task 6 stops and reports the run id and failing assertions to the coordinator; no fallback is designed up front): the lock-release test fails even once (no event exists for `LockFileEx` release), or a Node grandchild escapes even a `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`-only unit job.
- Gone on Windows rests on the screen and main process handles being signalled; the lock-release test (Step 1, test 5) proves that by then the holder's `LockFileEx` lock is free (V5 §6: the exit ordering is documented, the unlock timing only as best effort). `JOB_OBJECT_MSG_ACTIVE_PROCESS_ZERO` is only the post-Gone sweep's hint: nested child jobs (libuv's per-`node.exe` job, Codex's per-command jobs) post their zero messages under the unit's own completion key, so every zero message is confirmed by re-reading `JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation.ActiveProcesses` for the unit job before `wait_empty` completes, and the sweep keeps its `POST_GONE_EMPTY_WAIT` bound because delivery is not guaranteed (Stage 2: LB-08; V5 §3.7).
- The `__unit-exec` shim registers a console control handler so a Ctrl-C written to the pseudoconsole (by the user, or by Decision 11's soft interrupt) reaches the agent but never ends the shim (Stage 2: LB-08; V5 §3.2).
- Windows units are never retained across a server restart, as today (Stage 2: LB-26; R1; base detaches and records a sidecar only on Linux, `crates/freshell-codex/src/launch_lifecycle.rs:1203`, and never verifies one elsewhere, `sidecar_store.rs:363-366`): shutdown stops every unit, and `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` ends any member left when the server dies. Boot deletes records whose roots are verified gone and finishes the rest through their identity-verified roots and those roots' descendants. Crash path when kill-on-close has been cleared for a unit (Branch B's daemon join, or a stop that spares members in either branch; plan review R1-F3): from that moment the backend records every non-spared member in the unit record as a root with its start time — the job's process list at the clearing, then each `JOB_OBJECT_MSG_NEW_PROCESS` member, dropping each `JOB_OBJECT_MSG_EXIT_PROCESS` member (messages the port thread already receives; no polling) — so after a server crash the next boot finishes the record and reaches every member by identity-verified handle, plus their descendants by Toolhelp32 parent link (each child started after its parent). The only process this can miss is one started after the server died by a parent that then exited before the boot.
- WSL-mode panes on the Windows desktop app (pane shell `wsl`, or a Linux cwd: `crates/freshell-platform/src/spawn.rs:610-647` runs `wsl.exe --exec <cli>`) (Stage 2: LB-15):
  - Codex: the app-server sidecar is a Windows process (freshell-codex has no WSL path), so the agent and everything it starts are inside the Job Object; only the TUI screen runs in the distro behind a `wsl.exe` relay that is a job member, and the screen ends when the relay is terminated.
  - Every WSL-mode pane has members inside the distro, out of reach of a Job Object: the whole agent for Claude Code, Gemini, Kimi and terminal OpenCode, and the TUI for Codex. Decision (Stage 2: LB-15; Decision 11; plan review R2-F1): Linux containment inside the distro, with no new shipped binary, built by Task 23 on top of this backend. The relay spec runs the CLI through a short in-distro `sh` prelude that tags it and, when the distro runs a user manager the prelude can reach, places it in its own `systemd-run --user --scope` slice, else, when the distro has `perl`, runs it under the in-distro Perl reaper (plan review R3-F3); for a unit marked as having WSL members, this backend's `kill_all` makes one bounded in-distro kill call BEFORE it terminates anything (the slice when there is one, the reaper's tree when there is one, then every tagged process), then terminates the job's other members by handle and leaves the relay to exit on its own (plan review R3-F1). The `wsl.exe` relay is the unit's main and screen; Shift-X writes Ctrl-C into the PTY (Decision 11); Gone is the relay's own exit, which `wsl.exe --exec` makes only after the CLI inside the distro has exited, so Gone confirms the agent's death inside the distro; a relay that does not exit takes the unconfirmed path, and `TerminateJobObject` runs only after the relay has exited, for whatever Windows member is left.
  - Limit: only in a distro with neither a reachable user manager nor `perl` does the tag alone find members, so a detached process that clears its own environment can escape there; with either, the slice or the reaper's tree holds everything the CLI starts inside the distro, detached jobs included.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the design-decision runner tests (V5's early tests, before any backend code)**

These tests answer the open Windows questions on the runner, and Step 4's decision rule turns their outcome into the backend design (Stage 2: LB-08, LB-09, LB-10, LB-11; V5 §3.2, §4, §5, §6). The planned `windows_job.rs` tests are replaced (Step 5): their grandchild was `detached:true`, and libuv creates its job only on the first NON-detached spawn, so they could not detect LB-09; their daemon was a plain unit member with no breakaway, so they tested neither Codex's real launch nor server exit; and their lock holder only opened the file, so it could not detect a lock that outlives the holder.

First, the test helper `crates/freshell-containment/src/bin/freshell-test-helper.rs` (`[[bin]]` in the crate's `Cargo.toml`; test support only):
- `hold-lock <path> [--threads N] [--child]`: opens `<path>` with std `OpenOptions` (read, write, create) and calls `File::try_lock()`, exactly as Codex's `rollout/src/writer_lock.rs` takes the thread-writer lock (exit code 3 when it would block); starts N idle threads (they lengthen process teardown); with `--child`, starts a long-lived `idle` copy of itself; prints one line `locked <pid>`; exits normally when its stdin reaches end of file.
- `idle [args...]`: sleeps until killed and ignores its arguments, so `freshell-test-helper idle app-server --managed-daemon` is a daemon-family-shaped process for R7's predicate.
- `breakaway-daemon` (Windows only): starts a copy of itself as `idle app-server --managed-daemon` with `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` (Codex 0.162's exact daemon flags, V5 §5), prints `daemon <pid>` or `spawn-error <win32 error code>`, then sleeps until killed.

Then `crates/freshell-containment/tests/windows_decisions.rs` (`#![cfg(windows)]`). Every test creates its own named job with the flag set under test through windows-sys (the test holds the only handle), starts its first process through the `freshell-unit-exec` shim with `--job <that name>`, and first asserts (precondition) that this process is in the job (`IsProcessInJob`). It finds descendants by parent pid (`process::children`), opens a handle to every process it will wait on BEFORE acting, synchronises only on lines its children print (never on sleeps), and terminates by handle anything that ended up outside the job (an escaping process also escapes cargo's own job on the runner, V5 §3.5).

1. `node_grandchild_stays_in_unit_job` (job = `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` only; V5 §4): through the shim, `node -e` spawns non-detached `cmd.exe /d /c "ping -n 600 127.0.0.1 >NUL"` with `stdio: 'inherit'` (cmd models the native `codex.exe`, ping a shell command) and prints `ready`; a second case nests one more level (node → non-detached node → the same cmd → ping). Asserts `IsProcessInJob` is true for `cmd.exe` and `ping.exe` in both cases, and both handles are signalled within 10 s of `TerminateJobObject`.
2. `node_grandchild_stays_in_unit_job_with_breakaway_ok`: the same two cases and assertions with job = `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE | BREAKAWAY_OK`. This is LB-09's open question: whether a child silently breaking away from libuv's `SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK` job also leaves a parent job that has only `BREAKAWAY_OK` (V5 §4, F3–F4).
3. `a_node_launched_breakaway_daemon_leaves_a_breakaway_ok_unit` (job = `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE | BREAKAWAY_OK`; V5 §5): node → non-detached `freshell-test-helper breakaway-daemon`, and the helper started directly through the shim. Asserts the spawn printed `daemon <pid>`, `IsProcessInJob(daemon, job)` is false, and the daemon is still running after `TerminateJobObject` and after the test closes its job handle; cleanup by the daemon's handle.
4. `a_node_launched_breakaway_daemon_stays_in_a_kill_on_close_only_unit` (job = `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` only; V5 §5 NEW ASSUMPTIONS): the helper started directly prints `spawn-error 5` (`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`); through node, the spawn succeeds and the daemon IS in the job. Branch B relies on this.
5. `lockfileex_released_when_holder_handle_signals` (job = `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` only; V5 §6), 200 repetitions per variant: a non-detached node (mirroring `codex.js`) runs `freshell-test-helper hold-lock <tmp>/t.lock`; after `locked`, the test's own `File::try_lock` on that path answers `WouldBlock`; the test ends the holder and waits on the holder's handle; with no delay, `File::try_lock` from the test process and from a freshly started `hold-lock` process both succeed. Variants: `TerminateJobObject`; the holder's normal exit (its stdin closed); `TerminateProcess` of the holder alone; a holder with a live child (`--child`).
6. `the_shim_survives_ctrl_c_and_its_child_ends` (V5 §3.2): opens a ConPTY with portable-pty and spawns the shim (`--job`, a `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` job) running `cmd.exe /d /k ping -n 600 127.0.0.1`; once `ping.exe` exists, writes `\x03` to the PTY and asserts `ping.exe` exits within 10 s while the shim and `cmd.exe` keep running (the default control handler calls `ExitProcess` on the shim, so Freshell would see a screen exit while the agent runs on).

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the shim's Windows placement and control handler, and the Windows process facts**

These are the same in both branches, so they land before the decision.

`crates/freshell-containment/src/exec_shim.rs`:

```rust
use std::ffi::OsString;

/// `freshell-server __unit-exec [--job <name>] [--reaper] -- <program> [args...]`:
/// (Windows) put THIS process into the unit's job before anything else runs,
/// then run the command (it inherits the job, console/pseudoconsole and
/// stdio) and exit with its code. (Linux, `--reaper`) run the command under
/// Task 4's child-subreaper shim. Elsewhere it only runs the command.
pub fn unit_exec_main(args: Vec<OsString>) -> i32 {
    let mut job: Option<OsString> = None;
    let mut reaper = false;
    let mut it = args.into_iter();
    let mut rest: Vec<OsString> = Vec::new();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        if a == "--job" {
            job = it.next();
        } else if a == "--reaper" {
            reaper = true;
        } else if a == "--" {
            rest = it.collect();
            break;
        }
    }
    let Some((program, argv)) = rest.split_first() else { return 2 };
    #[cfg(windows)]
    if let Some(name) = job.as_ref() {
        if let Err(code) = windows_assign_self(name) {
            return code;
        }
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let _ = job;
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    if reaper {
        return crate::reaper::run(program, argv);
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
    let _ = reaper;
    match std::process::Command::new(program).args(argv).status() {
        Ok(s) => s.code().unwrap_or(1),
        Err(_) => 127,
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn windows_assign_self(name: &OsString) -> Result<(), i32> {
    use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, FALSE};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::JobObjects::{AssignProcessToJobObject, OpenJobObjectW, JOB_OBJECT_ASSIGN_PROCESS};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;
    let wide: Vec<u16> = name.encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect();
    unsafe {
        let job = OpenJobObjectW(JOB_OBJECT_ASSIGN_PROCESS, FALSE, wide.as_ptr());
        if job.is_null() {
            return Err(3);
        }
        let ok = AssignProcessToJobObject(job, GetCurrentProcess());
        CloseHandle(job);
        if ok == 0 { Err(4) } else { Ok(()) }
    }
}
```

Before running the command, the Windows shim registers a console control handler routine that returns TRUE for `CTRL_C_EVENT` and `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` (`SetConsoleCtrlHandler` with that routine and `TRUE`), so a Ctrl-C written to the pseudoconsole reaches the agent and never ends the shim. It must NOT call `SetConsoleCtrlHandler(NULL, TRUE)`: that ignore attribute is inherited by child processes and would disable Ctrl-C in the agent itself. If the handler cannot be registered, the shim exits with code 5 before spawning anything, like the job errors above (codes 3 and 4); R3 reports any of these as a typed placement failure with the wrapper's exit code. (Stage 2: LB-08; V5 §3.2)

Windows `process.rs` / `proc_watch.rs` bodies (same signatures as Linux):

```rust
// process.rs (cfg(windows))
use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, FILETIME, STILL_ACTIVE};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Process32FirstW, Process32NextW, PROCESSENTRY32W, TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{GetExitCodeProcess, GetProcessTimes, OpenProcess, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, PROCESS_VM_READ};

fn snapshot() -> Vec<(u32, u32)> { // (pid, parent)
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    unsafe {
        let snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0);
        let mut e: PROCESSENTRY32W = std::mem::zeroed();
        e.dwSize = std::mem::size_of::<PROCESSENTRY32W>() as u32;
        if Process32FirstW(snap, &mut e) != 0 {
            loop {
                out.push((e.th32ProcessID, e.th32ParentProcessID));
                if Process32NextW(snap, &mut e) == 0 { break; }
            }
        }
        CloseHandle(snap);
    }
    out
}
pub fn all_pids() -> Vec<u32> { snapshot().into_iter().map(|(p, _)| p).collect() }
pub fn parent(pid: u32) -> Option<u32> { snapshot().into_iter().find(|(p, _)| *p == pid).map(|(_, pp)| pp) }
pub fn children(pid: u32) -> Vec<u32> { snapshot().into_iter().filter(|(_, pp)| *pp == pid).map(|(p, _)| p).collect() }
pub fn start_time(pid: u32) -> std::io::Result<u64> {
    unsafe {
        let h = OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, 0, pid);
        if h.is_null() { return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound, "process gone")); }
        let (mut c, mut e, mut k, mut u): (FILETIME, FILETIME, FILETIME, FILETIME) = std::mem::zeroed();
        let ok = GetProcessTimes(h, &mut c, &mut e, &mut k, &mut u);
        CloseHandle(h);
        if ok == 0 { return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error()); }
        Ok(((c.dwHighDateTime as u64) << 32) | c.dwLowDateTime as u64)
    }
}
pub fn is_running(pid: u32) -> bool {
    unsafe {
        let h = OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, 0, pid);
        if h.is_null() { return false; }
        let mut code = 0u32;
        let ok = GetExitCodeProcess(h, &mut code);
        CloseHandle(h);
        ok != 0 && code == STILL_ACTIVE as u32
    }
}
/// Command line via NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessCommandLineInformation = 60),
/// split on whitespace (enough for the daemon-family token check).
pub fn argv(pid: u32) -> std::io::Result<Vec<String>> {
    use windows_sys::Wdk::System::Threading::NtQueryInformationProcess;
    unsafe {
        let h = OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ, 0, pid);
        if h.is_null() { return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error()); }
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64 * 1024];
        let mut len = 0u32;
        let status = NtQueryInformationProcess(h, 60, buf.as_mut_ptr().cast(), buf.len() as u32, &mut len);
        CloseHandle(h);
        if status != 0 { return Err(std::io::Error::other(format!("NtQueryInformationProcess {status:#x}"))); }
        let us = &*(buf.as_ptr() as *const windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::UNICODE_STRING);
        let s = String::from_utf16_lossy(std::slice::from_raw_parts(us.Buffer, (us.Length / 2) as usize));
        Ok(s.split_whitespace().map(str::to_string).collect())
    }
}
pub fn environ_value(_pid: u32, _key: &str) -> Option<String> { None } // not readable cross-process; the job is authoritative

// proc_watch.rs (cfg(windows)): Inner { identity, exited: AtomicBool, handle: SendHandle, done: tokio::sync::watch::Sender<bool>, waiter: std::sync::Once }
// open_inner: OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_TERMINATE); identity via start_time/argv;
//   expect_start mismatch -> NotFound.
// has_exited: WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0) == WAIT_OBJECT_0.
// exited: start (once) a std thread that blocks in WaitForSingleObject(handle, INFINITE) then sends `true`;
//   await the watch until true.
// signal: Kill -> TerminateProcess(handle, 1) (ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED after exit is Ok); Interrupt/Terminate -> Err(Unsupported).
```

The Windows process-name accessor (R9) returns the Toolhelp32 entry's `szExeFile` for that pid (the image file name, for example `codex.exe`); logs and the wire carry this name, never the command line `argv` reads (Stage 2: LB-46). `process::argv` is used only by the daemon-family predicate.

(The Windows `proc_watch.rs` body is written out in full by the implementer from the comments above; it has the same structure as the Linux version and is exercised by Task 2's two Windows `ProcWatch` tests in Steps 4 and 10.)

In `crates/freshell-server/src/main.rs`, before the tokio runtime exists (plan review R2-F1): `#[tokio::main] async fn main() -> ExitCode` becomes `async fn async_main() -> ExitCode`, called from a plain `fn main() -> ExitCode` whose first statements are the dispatch below and which then builds the runtime `#[tokio::main]` built (`tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().enable_all().build()`) and returns its `block_on(async_main())`. A shim lives as long as its pane, and the Linux reaper (Task 4) installs signal handlers and reaps with `waitpid(-1)`, so it must not carry a runtime's worker threads (one per CPU, in every pane's shim):

```rust
    if std::env::args_os().nth(1).is_some_and(|a| a == "__unit-exec") {
        std::process::exit(freshell_containment::exec_shim::unit_exec_main(std::env::args_os().skip(2).collect()));
    }
```

This dispatch runs before the server removes an inherited `FRESHELL_UNIT_ID` from its own environment (R1), so the shim passes the unit tag its placement set on to the command.

async fn lock_holders_and_listener_owner_are_found() {

A failure of either `SetInformationJobObject` call closes the job and returns the error (the planned code ignored both results; R2 forbids ignored fallible OS calls in the unit path).
- Reopening a recorded unit (R1's `Containment::reopen_unit`) does not look for a job: it yields a unit with no job whose `placement` errors (a reopened unit never gains members), whose `members` are the record's identity-verified roots that still run plus their descendants by Toolhelp32 parent link (each child's start time not earlier than its parent's), whose `kill_all` terminates those by handle, and whose `wait_empty` is `None` (R1, R3; plan review R1-F3). There is no `surviving()` (R1).
- `confirm_placement(pid)` (R3): opens the pid with `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION` and answers Ok only when `IsProcessInJob(handle, job)` is true.
- `spared(pids)`: every member whose OWN command line matches `is_codex_daemon_family` (R7), plus descendants of those by parent among the members (siblings are covered because each family member is matched on its own argv; V3 NA-1).
- `kill_all(roots)`: snapshot the members (`JobObjectBasicProcessIdList`) and the spared set. With no spared member and the unit not per-member: `TerminateJobObject` (Branch A always takes this path for a Codex pane). Otherwise: clear `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` if still set, mark the stop in progress (in Branch B the port thread then terminates late joiners; in both branches the post-Gone sweep runs `kill_all` once more), and terminate every non-spared member by handle, opening each target and checking `IsProcessInJob(handle, job)` before `TerminateProcess` so a pid reused between the snapshot and the open is never terminated; then `log_spared` (names and pids). This replaces the planned fixed 16-round re-enumeration loop.
- `remove()`: closes the job handle (kill-on-close ends any member still present; with kill-on-close cleared, spared members keep running) and removes the unit's entry from the port thread's map.

These items of the planned file stand as written (the remaining items of each `impl` are specified above):

```rust
struct SendHandle(HANDLE);
unsafe impl Send for SendHandle {}
unsafe impl Sync for SendHandle {}

fn job_name(id: &UnitId) -> String {
    format!("Local\\freshell-unit-{}", id.as_str())
}

fn wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
    s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
}

impl JobUnit {
    fn pids(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; 8 + 4096 * std::mem::size_of::<usize>()];
        let ok = unsafe {
            QueryInformationJobObject(self.job.0, JobObjectBasicProcessIdList, buf.as_mut_ptr().cast(), buf.len() as u32, std::ptr::null_mut())
        };
        if ok == 0 {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let list = unsafe { &*(buf.as_ptr() as *const JOBOBJECT_BASIC_PROCESS_ID_LIST) };
        let ids = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(list.ProcessIdList.as_ptr(), list.NumberOfProcessIdsInList as usize) };
        ids.iter().map(|p| *p as u32).collect()
    }
}

impl UnitBackend for JobUnit {
    fn placement(&self, _role: MemberRole, _seq: u32) -> io::Result<Placement> {
        let mut wrapper = vec![self.shim.exe.display().to_string()];
        wrapper.extend(self.shim.leading_args.iter().cloned());
        wrapper.extend(["--job".to_string(), self.name.clone(), "--".to_string()]);
        Ok(Placement { wrapper: Some(wrapper), env: vec![(UNIT_ENV.to_string(), self.id.as_str().to_string())] })
    }

    fn members(&self, _roots: &[u32]) -> io::Result<Vec<ProcIdentity>> {
        let pids = self.pids();
        let spared = self.spared(&pids);
        Ok(pids.into_iter().filter(|p| !spared.contains(p)).filter_map(|p| process::identity(p).ok()).collect())
    }

    fn wait_empty(&self) -> Option<BoxFuture<'static, ()>> {
        let mut rx = self.empty.clone();
        Some(Box::pin(async move {
            while !*rx.borrow() {
                if rx.changed().await.is_err() {
                    return;
                }
            }
        }))
    }
}
```

### Task 7: macOS tag backend facts (libproc facts and lookups, kqueue `ProcWatch`)

Design decisions (Stage 2: LB-11, LB-12, LB-26, LB-46; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V6.md`):
- V6's tests T1–T4 and the new T5 (plan review R1-F2) come first (Step 1) and run red on the macOS runners before any macOS body exists (Step 2).
- macOS releases a `flock` before it posts `NOTE_EXIT` (V6 §LB-11m(a)), but a process that has begun exiting is already invisible to `proc_find`: a late `EVFILT_PROC` registration, an `arg 0` `proc_pidinfo` lookup and `lsof` all report it gone while its files, and the lock, may still be open (V6 §LB-11m(b)). So `ProcWatch` concludes "exited" ONLY from a `NOTE_EXIT` on a registration made before the exit began, a zombie-aware lookup (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` with arg 1) showing `SZOMB`, or ESRCH from that zombie-aware lookup (reaped). ESRCH at registration means "exiting, not yet proven gone"; for a lock-holding member the wait continues on `EVFILT_VNODE`/`NOTE_FUNLOCK` on the unit's lock files.
- `lsof` is removed (it scans the whole host on every call, can be slow or block on a hung network mount, and skips exiting processes; V6 §LB-12(c)): lock holders and the listener come from libproc on the unit's members; outside holders scan same-uid processes.
- A same-uid process's environment is readable unless the kernel withholds it: on a Mac with SIP on, a target with `CS_RESTRICT` (the entitled official `node` and release `codex` binaries are likely candidates) returns argv only, silently (V6 §LB-12(b3)). Such a target is "environment withheld", never "untagged". The macOS CI test asserts SIP is enabled, otherwise it fails (on a SIP-off Mac every environment is readable and the test would pass falsely).
- Kernel-tracked membership, so a detached entitled job reparented to launchd (for example a `nohup node` or `setsid` dev server, environment withheld) is still killed by Shift-X (plan review R1-F2). Step 1's test T5 runs first on both macOS runners and picks the branch (decision rule in Step 2):
  - **Branch A (responsible process).** The macOS backend's placement wraps every member spawn in the shim: `[<shim exe>, <shim leading args...>, "--disclaim", "--"]`. With `--disclaim` the shim execs the command in place (`posix_spawn` with `POSIX_SPAWN_SETEXEC`, so the pane's spawned pid is the root) after `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim(attr, 1)`, making each root its own responsible process; the kernel copies a process's responsible pid to every child at fork and never changes it on reparenting, `setsid` or exec. Membership adds every same-uid process whose responsible pid (`responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid`) is a unit root's pid and whose start time is not earlier than that root's, counted only while that pid is still the pinned root (alive or a zombie) or is held by no live process, so a reused pid never makes a stranger a member. Both functions are private libSystem symbols resolved with `dlsym` (LLDB and Chromium resolve the disclaim one the same way); a missing symbol is Branch B. What can still escape: a process spawned with its own disclaim or launched by launchd on the agent's behalf (`open -a`, `launchctl submit`).
  - **Branch B (fork tracking), only if T5 fails.** One kqueue thread per unit with `EVFILT_PROC` `NOTE_FORK | NOTE_EXIT` registered on every member; each fork event triggers one one-shot scan (`proc_listallpids` plus the zombie-aware lookup) that adds every process whose parent, process group or session is a tracked pid, registers it the same way, and records it as a root in the unit record so a crash keeps it reachable. Branch B's `tokio_command` also starts every root as its own session leader (a `setsid()` in `pre_exec`; a PTY screen already leads its own session), so every descendant that never calls `setsid` stays findable by its session after its parent exits. What Branch B guarantees, stated as its contract (plan review R2-F2): a process is tracked when, at the scan that follows its parent's fork event, its parent, its process-group leader or its session leader is tracked; once tracked it stays a member until it exits, whatever its ancestors do. Residual, recorded and claimed by no test: a process in a session it or an ancestor created with `setsid`, whose session leader was never tracked because that leader's parent exited before the tracker handled the fork, when its environment is withheld (a readable one is still found by its tag). It is the platform's limit, not a design choice: kqueue's follow-across-fork `NOTE_TRACK` is refused with `ENOTSUP`, and Endpoint Security needs a restricted entitlement and root (Decision 4; plan review R3-F4).
- macOS units are never retained across a server restart, as today (Stage 2: LB-26; R1; base retains sidecars only on Linux, `crates/freshell-codex/src/launch_lifecycle.rs:1203`): shutdown stops every unit, and a record left by a crash is finished at boot through its roots, identity-verified with the libproc start time, and the kernel-tracked membership above.
- Logs and the wire carry a process's name, never its argv; `argv` stops after `argc` strings and never returns the environment that follows it in `KERN_PROCARGS2` (Stage 2: LB-46; R9; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V12.md` §LB-46a).

**Files:**
- Modify: `crates/freshell-containment/src/process.rs` (macOS: `all_pids` via `proc_listallpids`; `parent`/`is_running`/`start_time` and the process name via the zombie-aware `proc_pidinfo(pid, PROC_PIDTBSDINFO, 1, …)` (`pbi_ppid`, `pbi_status != SZOMB`, `pbi_start_tvsec * 1_000_000 + pbi_start_tvusec`, `pbi_name` or `pbi_comm`); `children` = `all_pids` filtered by parent; `argv` and the environment via `sysctl([CTL_KERN, KERN_PROCARGS2, pid])` bounded by its leading `argc`; `csops(pid, CS_OPS_STATUS)` for `CS_RESTRICT`; every OS: the tri-state environment reader `environ_read`, see **Interfaces**) (Stage 2: LB-12, LB-46)
- Modify: `crates/freshell-containment/src/proc_watch.rs` (macOS: `kqueue` + `EVFILT_PROC`/`NOTE_EXIT` registered at `open`; exit concluded only from the three proofs above; one blocking `kevent` thread per watch publishes to a `tokio::sync::watch`; `signal` = zombie-aware start-time re-check then `kill(2)`) (Stage 2: LB-11)
- Modify: `crates/freshell-containment/src/unit.rs` (macOS only: `set_lock_paths` also hands the paths to the unit's root watches, so a watch in the exiting state can wait on `NOTE_FUNLOCK`; the Gone lock check never opens a new `ProcWatch` on a holder after the kill; in Branch B, `tokio_command` also makes each root a session leader with `setsid()` in `pre_exec`, plan review R2-F2) (Stage 2: LB-11)
- Modify: `crates/freshell-containment/src/locks.rs` (macOS: libproc `PROC_PIDLISTFDS` + `proc_pidfdinfo(PROC_PIDFDVNODEPATHINFO)` with `FHASLOCK`), `src/listener.rs` (macOS: libproc `PROC_PIDFDSOCKETINFO` on the candidates) (Stage 2: LB-12)
- Modify: `crates/freshell-containment/src/backend/tag.rs` (membership reads the environment through `environ_read`; a withheld environment falls back to the kernel-tracked membership, roots and descendants and is logged; macOS placement adds the `--disclaim` shim wrapper in Branch A) (Stage 2: LB-12; plan review R1-F2)
- Modify: `crates/freshell-containment/src/exec_shim.rs` (macOS `--disclaim`: exec in place through `posix_spawn` with `POSIX_SPAWN_SETEXEC` after `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim`) and `src/process.rs` (macOS `responsible_pid(pid) -> Option<u32>` through `dlsym`); Branch B instead creates `src/backend/macos_forks.rs` (the per-unit fork tracker) (plan review R1-F2)
- Modify: `crates/freshell-containment/tests/conformance.rs`, `tests/unconfirmed.rs`, `tests/support/mod.rs` (`#![cfg(unix)]`; the agent script already uses `perl` for `setsid` and `flock`, see the note below)
- Modify: `.github/workflows/electron-build.yml` (Task 6's step becomes `- name: Test containment (Windows and macOS)` / `if: matrix.os != 'ubuntu-latest'`; before it, a macOS-only step (`if: startsWith(matrix.os, 'macos')`) installs the pinned npm package `@openai/codex@0.162.0` with npm into the runner's temp directory, outside the checkout so the pnpm tree is untouched, and exports through `$GITHUB_ENV` the path of the native `codex` binary that package's `codex.js` resolves for the runner's architecture as `FRESHELL_TEST_CODEX_NATIVE`) (Stage 2: LB-12)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 4 tag backend (R1 unit records; its membership now reads `environ_read`), Task 6's `freshell-test-helper hold-lock`, R9's `LockHolder { pid, name, path }` and the process-name accessor.

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn libproc_lookups_find_lock_file_holders_and_listeners() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let lock = dir.path().join("t.lock");
    std::fs::write(&lock, b"").unwrap();
    let mut holder = std::process::Command::new("perl")
        .args(["-e", "use Fcntl qw(:flock); open(my $f, '>>', $ARGV[0]) or die; flock($f, LOCK_EX); sleep 600", lock.to_str().unwrap()])

        .unwrap();

    let port = { let l = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap(); l.local_addr().unwrap().port() };

        .args(["-e", &format!("require('net').createServer().listen({port}, '127.0.0.1')")])
        .spawn()
        .unwrap();
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
    assert_eq!(listening_socket_owner(port, &[listener.id()]), Some(listener.id()));
    holder.kill().unwrap();
    listener.kill().unwrap();
}
