The first jump test also asserts that the reopen stack holds no entry for `'reopened'` once the duplicate's `closeTab` has settled (answer its `panes.closed` as `closeAndStopThunks.test.ts` does), so pressing "reopen closed tab" again reaches the tab closed before it; it fails without `dropReopenEntry` (Stage 2: finder §6). `tabsSlice.reopen.test.ts` gains `it('reopenClosedTab marks the reopened panes as user reopens', …)`: after `reopenClosedTab`, `isUserReopen` is true for the createRequestId of every terminal leaf in the restored layout (Stage 2: finder §6).

`pane-reconcile.test.ts`: `it('the stopped verdict folds to the stopped presentation and never respawns', …)` next to `:300`, and `it('a stopped verdict for a fresh-agent pane folds to its ended state and never re-creates', …)` — the fresh-agent pane's session is folded as exited and no `freshAgent.create` is sent (Stage 2: LB-42).

Expected: FAIL — the stopped attach re-creates; the reconcile verdict `stopped` is unhandled for both pane kinds; `markUserReopen` does not exist; Reopen from the stopped bar keeps the killed createRequestId; the jumped-from duplicate stays on the reopen stack.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the minimal production implementation**

As listed under **Files**. The jump fold (shared by `terminal.created` and the `RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`+`liveTerminalId` refusal):

```ts
export function jumpToHolderIfUserReopen(dispatch: AppDispatch, state: RootState, createRequestId: string, holderTerminalId: string): boolean {
  if (!isUserReopen(createRequestId)) return false
  clearUserReopen(createRequestId)
  const holder = selectTabPaneByTerminalId(state, holderTerminalId)
  const mine = findPaneByCreateRequestId(state, createRequestId)
  if (!holder || !mine || (holder.tabId === mine.tabId && holder.paneId === mine.paneId)) return false
  const layout = state.panes.layouts[mine.tabId]
  if (layout?.type === 'leaf') {
    void dispatch(closeTab(mine.tabId)) // a plain close: nothing is killed
  } else {
    void dispatch(closePaneWithCleanup({ tabId: mine.tabId, paneId: mine.paneId }))
  }
  dispatch(setActiveTab(holder.tabId))
  dispatch(setActivePane({ tabId: holder.tabId, paneId: holder.paneId, focusNudge: true }))
  return true
}
```

In the whole-tab branch, once that `closeTab` has settled and the tab is gone, the fold dispatches `dropReopenEntry({ tabId: mine.tabId })`, so the duplicate never sits on the reopen stack (Stage 2: finder §6). The exit banner's stopped-presentation Reopen mints the new createRequestId, marks it with `markUserReopen`, and dispatches `resetPaneForReconcileCreate({ tabId, paneId, intent: 'respawn', sessionRef, createRequestId })` (Stage 2: LB-36).

```rust
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn a_stopping_owner_frame_precedes_the_vacant_one() {
    let h = UnitHarness::start(HarnessOpts::default()).await;
    let mut ws = h.connect().await;
    let tid = h.create_codex(&mut ws, "crq-sf", Some("t-sf")).await;
    h.send(&mut ws, kill(Some(&tid), "crq-sf", "rs")).await;
    let first = h.next_matching(&mut ws, Duration::from_secs(10), |f| f["type"] == "session.runtimeOwner" && f["sessionId"] == "t-sf").await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first["transition"], "stopping");
    let second = h.next_matching(&mut ws, Duration::from_secs(10), |f| f["type"] == "session.runtimeOwner" && f["sessionId"] == "t-sf").await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(second["ownerKind"], "vacant");
}
```

(The test also asserts that `first["stoppingSince"]` is a number; Stage 2: LB-34.)

Rotation shifts `.1 … .N` up by one and moves the active file to `.1` as today; it then deletes, oldest first, every backup past `min_backups` whose modification time (the time of its newest line: a rotated file is never written again) is older than `window`; then, while the active file and the backups together exceed `max_total_bytes`, it deletes the oldest backup and records an alert when that file is younger than `window`. `create(path, max_bytes, max_backups, secret)` keeps its exact behaviour as `create_with_retention` with `Retention { min_backups: max_backups, window: Duration::ZERO, max_total_bytes: u64::MAX }`, so the supervisor and session-host writers are unchanged.

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: the retention API listed under Files (plan review R2-F4); otherwise this task proves the schema. Retention is a time property: every line of the last 24 hours is kept at any volume below the 1 GiB cap, and only the cap can cut that short, with an ERROR. For scale (`plan-automation-activity-logging.md` §4.2): non-HTTP volume is at most 76 KB/h, about 1.8 MB a day, once HTTP 2xx lines (96.6% of today's volume) no longer reach the default `info` filter; a flood of 4xx lines would need about 40 lines a second (at about 300 bytes a line) for a whole day to reach the cap.

#[path = "support/server_proc.rs"]
mod server_proc;

fn events(home: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<Value> {
    std::fs::read_to_string(home.join("logs/rust-server.jsonl")).unwrap_or_default()
        .lines().filter_map(|l| serde_json::from_str(l).ok()).filter(|v: &Value| v["target"] == "freshell_unit").collect()
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn a_shift_x_and_a_reopen_log_the_full_keyed_sequence() {
    let home = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let mut s = start(home.path(), &[("FAKE_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BEHAVIOR", "{}"), ("FRESHELL_LOG_DIR", home.path().join("logs").to_str().unwrap())]);
    assert!(wait_for_health(s.port, &mut s.child, Duration::from_secs(30)).await);
    let (mut ws, tid) = create_resume(s.port, "crq-log", "t-log").await;
    send_json(&mut ws, &json!({"type": "terminal.kill", "terminalId": tid, "requestId": "rk", "createRequestId": "crq-log"})).await;
    send_json(&mut ws, &json!({"type": "terminal.create", "requestId": "crq-log2", "mode": "codex", "shell": "system", "restore": true,
        "sessionRef": {"provider": "codex", "sessionId": "t-log"}})).await;
    wait_for_message_type(&mut ws, "terminal.created", Duration::from_secs(20)).await.unwrap();
    let ev = events(home.path());
    let names: Vec<&str> = ev.iter().filter(|e| e["terminal_id"] == tid.as_str()).map(|e| e["event"].as_str().unwrap()).collect();
    let pos = |n: &str| names.iter().position(|x| *x == n).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{n} missing in {names:?}"));
    assert!(pos("unit.stop.requested") < pos("unit.stop.signal_sent"));
    assert!(pos("unit.stop.signal_sent") < pos("unit.stop.gone"));
    let gone = ev.iter().find(|e| e["event"] == "unit.stop.gone" && e["terminal_id"] == tid.as_str()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(gone["level"], "INFO");
    assert_eq!(gone["lock_released"], true);
    assert!(gone["duration_ms"].as_u64().is_some());
    for key in ["unit_id", "provider", "session_id", "terminal_id", "operation_id"] {
        assert!(gone[key].as_str().is_some_and(|v| !v.is_empty()), "{key} keyed");
    }
    let requested = ev.iter().find(|e| e["event"] == "unit.stop.requested" && e["terminal_id"] == tid.as_str()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((requested["reason"].as_str(), requested["mode"].as_str()), (Some("shift-x"), Some("force")));
    assert!(ev.iter().any(|e| e["event"] == "unit.start.waited" && e["session_id"] == "t-log"), "time spent waiting before the reopen");
    unsafe { libc::kill(s.child.id() as i32, libc::SIGKILL) };
}

```markdown
### Closing tabs and stopping agents

A plain close (the tab's **×**, `Alt+W`, or a pane's **×**) hides the tab but leaves its agent running in the background. The sidebar marks agents that are running in the background, and reopening the tab (`Alt+Shift+T` / `Alt+H`) or clicking the session in the sidebar attaches to the same running agent. Reopening never stops anything.

To stop an agent, **Shift+click** the tab's or pane's **×**, or right-click the tab or pane and choose **Close and stop agent** (keyboard: focus the tab or the pane and press `Shift+F10` or the Menu key). Freshell stops the agent and everything it started — including commands it left running in the background — and closes the tab once the agent is confirmed gone, so you can reopen the same conversation right away. If stopping takes more than a few seconds, the tab shows **Stopping…** until it finishes. One limit: on macOS, and for agents that run inside a WSL distribution that has neither systemd nor Perl in the Windows desktop app, a background command that detaches itself in unusual ways can survive the stop.

To stop an agent that is running in the background, click it in the sidebar to open it, then Shift+click its **×** (or use **Close and stop agent**). Background agents that have been really idle for 24 hours — not working, nothing queued, and not waiting for you — are stopped automatically. This covers Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Amplifier, Gemini and Kimi. Programs you add as CLI extensions are not asked: once their tab is closed, they are stopped after showing no activity for the **Auto-kill idle (minutes)** setting (15 minutes by default), the same as plain shell tabs.

When another device stops an agent, that pane shows it as stopped instead of starting it again. If a conversation is open in another program (for example `codex` in a shell), Freshell tells you which program holds it, by its process number and name.
```

### Task 33: Opt-in real-Codex contract — SIGINT and SIGKILL release the writer lock and resume works

**Files:**

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the real Codex 0.162 CLI. The test always uses a fresh isolated temporary `CODEX_HOME`. An unauthenticated isolated home accepts `initialize` + `thread/start`, and the native app-server holds the thread's writer lock from `thread/start` on (Stage 2: LB-41; `<logs_dir>/reports/load-bearing-validator-V8.md` §41a, §41b). `FRESHELL_REAL_CODEX_HOME` and the archive step are dropped. The user's `CODEX_HOME` is never used, so the test can never leave a real lock there, and `auth.json` is never read or copied (Stage 2: LB-41; finder §6 Task 33).
- Produces: a contract that proves the two signals the stop sequence relies on, against the real binary. It also pins the answer that the entry points' "never materialized → start new" rule detects: `thread/resume` of a turnless thread answers `-32600` "no rollout found" (Stage 2: LB-41).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing behavioral test**

The planned code block is replaced by the specification below (Stage 2: LB-41). The planned test could not pass and could leave a real app-server behind:
- A turnless thread has no rollout to resume after SIGINT or SIGKILL (`-32600 "no rollout found for thread id …"`, V8 §41c). Resume works once a model-free `thread/shellCommand` has materialized the thread (V8 §41e).
- A bare isolated home makes outbound HTTPS calls (Responses prewarm, plugin clone; V8 §41a).
- The planned `afterAll` SIGKILLed only the launchers, which orphans each native app-server (`codex.js` forwards only the first signal).
- Signals went to pids without a start-time pin (Global Constraint 73).
- `untilDead` treated a zombie as alive.
- The `// @vitest-environment node` directive was missing (finder §6 Task 33).

V8's driver was executed and is the basis for the request shapes below (`<logs_dir>/scratch/V8/drive.mjs`, `start_as.sh`, `lb41.sh`; report §1 and §41a–e).

These two helpers stay exactly as planned:

```ts
function freePort(): number {
  const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['-e', "const s=require('net').createServer().listen(0,'127.0.0.1',()=>{console.log(s.address().port);s.close()})"], { encoding: 'utf8' })
  return Number(r.stdout.trim())
}

function nativePid(port: number): number {
  const out = spawnSync('ss', ['-Hltnp', `sport = :${port}`], { encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout
  return Number(/pid=(\d+)/.exec(out)?.[1])
}
```

The rest of the file:
- **Header.** The file starts with `// @vitest-environment node`, as the Amplifier contracts in the same directory do.
- **Home.** Each test gets a fresh temporary `CODEX_HOME` containing a `config.toml`.
  - The config selects a loopback-only model provider, as V8 §1 item 6 did: a provider named in `model_provider` whose `base_url` is an unused `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1` and whose `wire_api` is `responses`. No model request can leave the host, and the Responses prewarm is off.
  - The same file turns off the `plugins` feature (codex-rs 0.162 `features/src/lib.rs:1559-1560`; read from source, not executed by any validator).
  - Any remaining unauthenticated outbound traffic is accepted for this opt-in test, because the home holds no credentials and nothing costs money. That covers Codex's start-up `git ls-remote`, and the plugin clone if the switch does not stop it.
- **App-servers.** Start each with `spawn('codex', ['-c', 'features.apps=false', 'app-server', '--listen', 'ws://127.0.0.1:<freePort()>'], { env: { ...process.env, CODEX_HOME }, stdio: 'ignore' })` (V8's launch shape; the URL carries no path). The RPC client keeps the planned shape: it connects to the same path-less URL with a bounded retry, sends `initialize` with `capabilities.experimentalApi: true` and then `initialized`. It also hands notifications to waiters, which the planned client dropped.
- **Identities.** Once the listener is up, `nativePid(port)` names the native. Before any signal, the test checks that the native descends from the launcher it spawned (following parent pids in `/proc/<pid>/stat`), and it pins the native's start time (field 22). Every signal re-checks that start time first.
- **Exited.** A process has exited when `/proc/<pid>` is absent, its state is `Z`, or its start time differs from the pinned one. The test never uses `kill(pid, 0)`, which a zombie still answers.
- **Lock checks.** The lock file is `<CODEX_HOME>/thread-writer-locks/<thread>.lock`.
  - Held: a non-blocking `flock -x -n <file> true` exits non-zero, and the native has an fd on that file whose `/proc/<native>/fdinfo/<fd>` has a `lock:` line. This is fd attribution (Task 3; V8 checked holders the same way).
  - Free: the file is absent (a graceful SIGINT exit unlinks it, V8 §41d), or the non-blocking `flock` succeeds.
- **Cleanup that never orphans a real app-server.** In each test's `finally` and again in `afterAll`, every app-server the test started is stopped:
  1. SIGKILL the pinned native if it is still the same process.
  2. Then signal the launcher.
  3. Wait (bounded) until both have exited.
  4. Only then remove the temporary home.
- **Cases** (each `it` has a 60 s timeout and its own home):
  1. and 2. `SIGINT` / `SIGKILL` to the native app-server releases the lock, and a new app-server resumes:
     1. Start app-server A.
     2. Send `thread/start` `{ cwd, approvalPolicy: 'never', sandbox: 'danger-full-access' }`.
     3. Send `thread/shellCommand` `{ threadId, command: 'echo materialize' }` and await `turn/completed` for that thread.
     4. The lock is held by the native. Send the signal to the native and wait until it has exited. The lock is free.
     5. Start app-server B. `thread/resume` `{ threadId }` answers without an error, and B's native now holds the lock.
  3. A turnless thread is not resumable: the same steps without the shell command, with SIGINT. After the native exits, the lock is free, and B's `thread/resume` answers error code `-32600` with a message containing `no rollout found`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing behavioral test**

`test/integration/electron/agent-unit-kill-reopen.test.ts`:

The planned code block is replaced by the specification below. The planned evidence could not fail correctly (Stage 2: LB-48):
- It asserted every launcher and native pid dead at the kill acknowledgement. Gone does not wait for descendants, a zombie still answers `kill(pid, 0)`, and `TerminateJobObject` completes asynchronously, so that assertion would flake.
- It waited for a JSON "listening" line, but the startup line is plain text.
- It authenticated with another test's token (finder §6 Task 34).

The test, `describe('desktop app: kill then reopen a Codex pane')` with `it('stops the whole agent and reopens the same conversation without a conflict')` and a 120 s timeout, does the following:
1. **Setup** (plan review R1-F9: the desktop app, not a directly spawned server):
   - A temp home (`freshell-unit-smoke-` prefix) with a `manifests` dir and a free port; `<home>/.freshell/.env` holds a throwaway `AUTH_TOKEN`, and `<home>/.freshell/desktop.json` selects the app's own server: `{ serverMode: 'app-bound', port: <free port>, knownServers: [], alwaysAskOnLaunch: false, setupCompleted: true, startOnLogin: false, minimizeToTray: false }` (the shape `test/e2e-electron/app-bound-rust-server.test.ts:394-411` writes).
   - The fixtures in `test/fixtures/coding-cli/codex-app-server/`.
   - A dispatcher in the home. On Unix it is `codex`, a bash script that execs `node fake-codex-launcher.mjs "$@"` when the arguments contain `app-server` and `node fake-codex-tui.mjs "$@"` otherwise. On Windows it is `codex.cmd`, which does the same as an if/else, so a launcher that exits non-zero never falls through to the TUI branch.
   - The app is launched with `_electron.launch({ executablePath: <the unpacked app executable>, env })`, where `env` is `isolatedElectronHomeEnv(process.env, <home>)` plus `FRESHELL_ELECTRON_TEST_NO_LOCAL_DISCOVERY=1`, `CODEX_HOME=<home>/.codex`, `CODEX_CMD=<dispatcher>`, `FAKE_CODEX_MANIFEST_DIR=<manifests>`, `FAKE_CODEX_APP_SERVER_ALLOW_DURABLE_WRITES=1` and `FAKE_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BEHAVIOR={"spawnHelperProcess":true}` (so the native has a descendant of its own). The app's server child inherits that environment (`electron/server-spawner.ts:238-257`) and gets `FRESHELL_HOME=<home>/.freshell`, so its unit records are its own and its boot touches nothing else on the machine (Stage 2: LB-01). If the launch chooser appears anyway, the test chooses "Start local", as the app-bound test does (`:457-461`).
2. **Readiness.** The app window navigates to `http://localhost:<port>`; `GET /api/health` answers 200 through `requestJson`'s bounded retry; the window shows the tab bar.
3. **Create.** `POST /api/tabs` with the token, `{ mode: 'codex', shell: 'system', sessionRef: { provider: 'codex', sessionId: 't-smoke' } }` (agent-created, so focus-neutral), then click the new tab in the app window (by role and name) and wait until that pane's terminal shows `FAKE_TUI_READY thread=t-smoke` (read through `GET /api/panes/<pane>/capture`), so the native holds the writer lock before the kill. On native Windows, `shell: 'system'` resolves to `cmd` (`crates/freshell-platform/src/spawn.rs:146-153`), so this pane runs natively, not in WSL.
4. **Identities.** Read every manifest. There are at least two (`launcher-<pid>.json` and `native-<pid>.json`). The native is the main. The launcher and the pids in the native manifest's `children` are the descendants checked in step 8. On Linux, pin each pid's start time from `/proc/<pid>/stat`.
5. **Lock held before the kill.** The lock file is `<CODEX_HOME>/thread-writer-locks/t-smoke.lock`.
   - Linux: util-linux `flock -x -n <file> true` exits non-zero.
   - Windows: a fresh instance of Task 1's `LockFileEx` holder on that path reports that it could not take the lock.
   - macOS: no OS lock (see **Interfaces**).
6. **Kill, in the app.** Shift+click the tab's close button (located by role and accessible name, never by CSS selector). The tab stays until the server confirms Gone (Shift-X acknowledges only at Gone); wait, bounded at 10 s, for the tab to disappear from the tab bar.
7. **When the tab has closed, with no further waiting** (Stage 2: LB-48):
   - The native main has exited. Linux: `/proc/<pid>/stat` is absent, or its state is `Z`, or its start time differs from the pinned one. Windows: `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws, because libuv reports ESRCH once the exit code is set. macOS: `ps -o stat= -p <pid>` is empty or starts with `Z`.
   - The writer lock is free: the lock file is absent, or the same real lock attempt as in step 5 now succeeds (Windows: the fresh holder takes the lock and the test then stops that holder).
   - The launcher and descendants are NOT asserted here.
8. **After the post-Gone sweep.** Within a 10 s test-only bounded wait, every recorded launcher and descendant pid has exited by the same per-OS test.
9. **Reopen, in the app.** Press Shift+Alt+T in the app window (the reopen shortcut, `src/lib/tab-switch-shortcuts.ts:26-27`). The reopened tab's pane gets a different terminal id, and the first output of that terminal matching `/FAKE_TUI_READY|open in another app/` (read through the capture route) contains `FAKE_TUI_READY thread=t-smoke`.
10. **Second kill, through the right-click item.** Right-click the reopened tab and choose "Close and stop agent" (by role `menuitem` and name); the tab closes, and steps 7–8's checks hold for the reopened native.
11. **Cleanup, on every path.**
    1. If a Codex tab is still open, stop it through the REST kill route and await its answer before closing the app. Otherwise Linux keep-on-restart retention would keep its sidecar running after the test.
    2. Close the app with `closeElectronGracefully`, then verify its server child stopped with the owned-server teardown helpers (the app-bound test's pattern).
    3. Within a bounded wait, every pid named by any manifest has exited.
    4. Nothing else is ever signalled.

Why it fails before the change: on the base commit, a Shift+click closes the tab at once while the native app-server is still running and holding the writer lock (defects 1, 2 and 12), and on Windows the native is orphaned outright, so the main-exited assertion at the tab's close fails.

A second case, `it('stops a WSL-mode agent pane and every job it started in the distro')` (Stage 2: LB-15), runs only on Windows when a WSL distro answers `wsl.exe --exec true`. Otherwise it skips with that reason. The `windows-2022` runner is expected to skip it (no distro is installed there), and DANDESKTOP is expected to run it.
- **What it exercises.** WSL-mode containment (Decision 11; plan review R2-F1, R3-F1, R3-F3): the relay spec runs the CLI through the in-distro prelude (its own `systemd-run --user --scope` slice when the distro has a reachable user manager, else the Perl reaper when the distro has `perl`, the unit tag always); Shift-X writes Ctrl-C into the PTY; the one-shot in-distro call kills the slice, the reaper's tree and every tagged process before anything is terminated; Gone is the relay's own exit.
- **The distro-side fake.** The case writes a bash script into its temp home, which the distro reads through `/mnt/<drive>/…`. The script records its own pid, start time and `$FRESHELL_UNIT_ID`, starts one ordinary `sleep` child and one detached `setsid nohup sleep` job, records both pids and start times, and waits. Before creating the pane, the case asks the distro once (`wsl.exe --exec sh -c` with the prelude's probe, plus `command -v perl`) whether it has a reachable user manager or `perl`; when it has either, the script also starts Task 4's `envless_job` shape (a detached job that execs `env -i sleep 600` once its parent is gone) and records its pid and start time.
- **The pane.** A `mode: 'claude'`, `shell: 'wsl'` pane with `CLAUDE_CMD` set to the script's distro path. The screen runs as `wsl.exe --exec sh -c <WSL_UNIT_EXEC_SH> sh <unit id> <script>` (`spawn.rs:621-648` plus Task 23's prelude).
- **Assertions.**
  - First, without Freshell, the assumption Gone rests on (plan review R3-F1): `wsl.exe --exec sh -c 'exec 0<&- 1>&- 2>&-; sleep 5; exit 7'` started by the test exits with code 7 and no earlier than 5 s after it started, so a relay does not end while its in-distro process lives, even one that closed its stdio. If this fails, the case fails with that message, and the coordinator reopens Decision 11.
  - The script's recorded `FRESHELL_UNIT_ID` is a unit id (`u` + 32 hex).
  - The kill acknowledgement has `success === true`, and the first `/proc/<pid>/stat` read the case makes after it shows the script itself (the CLI) already exited (plan review R3-F1).
  - Within one 10 s bounded wait after the acknowledgement, the script, its ordinary child AND the detached `setsid nohup sleep` job have all exited. This is checked from the distro with `wsl.exe --exec` reads of `/proc/<pid>/stat` by recorded pid and start time.
  - With a user manager in the distro, the `envless_job` has exited too, within the same wait, and the log line below says `tier: "slice"`; without one but with `perl`, the same holds with `tier: "reaper"`; with neither it says `tier: "tag"`, and the run state records that DANDESKTOP's distro gets the tag tier (whose stated limit is the job this case then does not start).
  - The server log has an INFO `unit.wsl_members_killed` for that unit that names processes by pid and name only.
  - If an assertion fails, the case stops any of its recorded processes that is still alive (after re-checking the start time; it started them) before it fails.
- **Why no Codex WSL-mode case.** Codex is not exercised this way: one `CODEX_CMD` names both the Windows sidecar and the distro-side screen, so no fake can serve both sides.

## Plan revision notes (plan review round 2)

- Fresh Eyes round 2 returned four Major findings and one Minor; each change is tagged `plan review R2-Fn`. The `## User Request` block is unchanged; task numbering is unchanged (34 tasks).
- F1: the Linux fallback (no user manager) keeps membership by the kernel: every member starts under the `__unit-exec --reaper` child-subreaper shim, so every orphaned descendant stays in its pane's tree whatever it does to its environment; the server dispatches the shim before building its tokio runtime (Decision 19, Tasks 4 and 6). Checked on this host first with a stand-in under a PTY (`<logs_dir>/scratch/subreaper/run1.txt`). WSL-mode panes get a `systemd-run --user --scope` slice inside the distro when it has a reachable user manager, the tag otherwise, and the in-distro kill spares the Codex daemon family (Decision 11, Tasks 6, 23, 34).
- F2: macOS Branch B states what fork tracking guarantees (roots are session leaders; a process whose parent, group leader or session leader is tracked at the scan is tracked); `a_detached_entitled_job_is_killed_by_a_stop` asserts both jobs dead unconditionally in both branches, with Branch B's intermediates gated to exactly that guarantee, and the race outside it is a stated residual (Decision 4, Task 7).
- F3: every stopped-pane record has its own file; fresh-agent records are keyed by the createRequestId bound at each stop, so kill, reopen and kill again keeps both ids across restarts (Decision 10, Task 18).
- F4: log retention is by age: rotated files are deleted only once older than the 24-hour cleanup window, two backups are always kept, and only a 1 GiB disk-safety cap can delete a younger file, with an ERROR; the tests set file ages instead of assuming a volume (Decision 16, Task 30).
- F5: the README names Gemini and Kimi among the agents the 24-hour rule stops, and moves a CLI out of that list if Task 22 Step 1 finds its hooks cannot be supplied per pane (Task 31).
- New assumption to validate during execution: inside a WSL distro that runs systemd, `systemctl --user` and `systemd-run --user --scope` answer from a `wsl.exe --exec` process; the prelude probes this at each start and falls back to the tag, and Task 34's DANDESKTOP case records which tier the user's distro gets.
